# Start a Session

Entry point for the isthmia workflow. A **session** is one git worktree, one branch, one batch of work, and one pull request at the end.

Your job is to orchestrate, not to disappear into a task. The user treats this session like a browser main thread. Keep it free.

## Companion skills

Each step of the workflow is its own skill. Call them, do not re-implement them.

| Skill               | When                                            |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `capture`           | File a GitHub issue                             |
| `triage`            | Clean up the issue backlog                      |
| `design`            | Tier 3 — write a design doc and get it approved |
| `implement`         | Tier 2 and 3 — brief and dispatch a sub-agent   |
| `review`            | Review the session diff                         |
| `end-session`       | Verify, review, and open the PR                 |
| `technical-writing` | Any prose you write                             |

## 1. Open the session

Every session runs in its own **git worktree**. The user runs sessions in parallel in separate terminals, and a worktree is what keeps them from fighting over one working tree.

Do this once, at the start.

1. **Check where you are.** Run `git status --short` and `git branch --show-current`.
   - Already in a session worktree — use it. Do not nest worktrees.
   - The tree is dirty with unrelated changes — ask the user what to do first.
   - On a branch that is not `main` in the main checkout — ask whether to continue there or open a fresh worktree.

2. **Pick a name.** Propose a short slug for the work, such as `roster-reports` or `auth-cleanup`. Fall back to `session-YYYY-MM-DD` when the session has no theme yet. Confirm it with the user.

3. **Create the worktree and the branch together**, so the branch gets a real name:

   ```sh
   git fetch origin
   git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<slug> -b session/<slug> origin/main
   ```

   Then enter it with `EnterWorktree`, passing `path: .claude/worktrees/<slug>`.

   Creating the worktree with `EnterWorktree`'s `name` argument also works, but it names the branch `worktree-<slug>`, which reads badly in the pull request.

4. **Set the worktree up.** A new worktree has no dependencies and no git hooks:

   ```sh
   direnv allow    # generates .pre-commit-config.yaml from git-hooks.nix
   just install    # pnpm install, this worktree only
   ```

   Skip `direnv allow` and commits will fail with "No .pre-commit-config.yaml file was found".

5. **Start a task list** with `TodoWrite`. It becomes the PR body at the end of the session.

6. Tell the user the session is open and name the worktree path. They can now describe tasks one at a time.

Never repeat this step. One worktree and one branch per session.

## 2. Triage each request into a tier

The user describes something they want. Decide how big it is **before** you touch anything. Read the relevant code first — a two-minute read prevents a wrong tier.

State the tier you chose in one line, then act. Do not ask the user to confirm the tier. If you get it wrong, change tiers mid-task and say so.

### Tier 1 — do it inline

The change is small, obvious, and local. One or two files. No design choice to make.

Examples: a typo, a rename, a wrong constant, a missing `.js` import extension, a doc tweak, a one-line bug fix with an obvious cause.

Do it yourself, now. Run `just check`. Commit it. Report in two lines. Dispatching a sub-agent for this costs more than doing it.

### Tier 2 — clarify, then dispatch

The change is real work but the approach is not in doubt. It touches one package, or several files in a clear pattern.

Examples: add a test suite for a module, fix a bug that needs a regression test, refactor a function and its callers, add a CLI flag.

1. Ask only the questions whose answers change the work. Zero questions is common. Cap it at one round.
2. Find the exact `path:line` anchors yourself.
3. Call `implement` to brief and dispatch the sub-agent.
4. Stay available while it runs.

### Tier 3 — design first

The change needs a decision, spans packages, touches infrastructure or auth, or deserves more than one review cycle.

Examples: a new package, a schema change, an auth model change, anything in `packages/infrastructure` that changes topology.

1. Call `design`. It writes a doc to `.claude/plans/` and waits for the user to approve it.
2. File an issue with `capture` **only if** the work will span more than this session. Otherwise the design doc is enough.
3. After approval, call `implement` once per implementation step.

Tier 3 work lands on the session branch like everything else. It does not get its own PR.

## 3. Stay responsive

One sub-agent writes to the tree at a time. Two concurrent writers will collide on a shared branch.

The worktree isolates this session from the user's _other_ sessions. It does not isolate your sub-agents from each other — they all share this worktree.

While a sub-agent runs, you are still free. Do this:

- Answer the user's questions, read code, and explain things.
- Plan the next task and find its anchors.
- Run read-only commands.
- Dispatch read-only research sub-agents (`Explore`) if it helps.

Do not do this:

- Edit a file, commit, or dispatch a second writing sub-agent. Queue that work and say it is queued.

When the sub-agent returns, run `git show --stat HEAD`, read the diff if it is non-trivial, and give the user a short summary. Tick the task off the list.

If the work is wrong, dispatch a follow-up sub-agent or revert the commit. Do not patch it by hand.

## 4. End the session

When the user says they are done, call `end-session`.

## Guardrails

- One worktree, one branch, one PR, one writer at a time.
- **Never run bare `git stash`.** The stash stack is shared with every other worktree and every parallel session. A `git stash pop` here can swallow another session's work. Make a temporary commit instead.
- Never push to `main`. Never merge a PR. The human merges, and that merge is the approval.
- Keep each commit scoped to one task, so a bad one can be reverted on its own.
- Unrelated problems found mid-task — tell the user or run `capture`. Never widen the diff.
- If a tier-2 task turns out to need a design decision, stop it and move to tier 3.
I'll start by checking where we are.

# @cyc-seattle/clubspot-sync

A Cloud Run job that syncs one Clubspot club's camps, schedule, and registrations into the CRM's
Directus instance (`@cyc-seattle/crm`). Replaces the spreadsheet-backed reports in
`admin-functions` for that data. See issue #70.

## Running locally

Start a local Directus and Postgres with `just directus-local` from the repository root. It
applies `packages/crm/schema.yaml` to a fresh instance.

Then run the CLI against it:

```sh
CLUBSPOT_EMAIL=... CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD=... \
DIRECTUS_URL=http://localhost:8055 DIRECTUS_TOKEN=... \
pnpm exec clubspot-sync --club <clubspot-club-id> --dry-run
```

Options:

- `--club <id>` - the Clubspot club id to sync (env `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID`)
- `--directus-url <url>` - the base URL of the CRM's Directus instance (env `DIRECTUS_URL`)
- `--directus-token <token>` - a Directus static token for the sync's machine user (env
  `DIRECTUS_TOKEN`)
- `--dry-run` - log the writes the sync would make, without making them
- `--camp <id>` - sync only this camp, bypassing discovery and change detection
- `--since <iso-date>` - backfill: re-read `--camp`'s registrations from this date instead of its
  stored watermark. Requires `--camp`.

Prefer the env vars over `--directus-token` and the Clubspot password flags. A flag value is
visible to anyone on the box who runs `ps` (#49).

## Verifying and backfilling one camp

`--camp <id>` syncs a single camp on demand, bypassing discovery and the backoff check - useful for
checking one camp's data or re-running it right after a mapping fix.

On its own, `--camp` still filters registrations to the camp's stored watermark (its last
successful sync), so re-running it against an already-synced camp only picks up recent changes.
To re-read further back - for a backfill after a mapping fix, say - add `--since <iso-date>` to
widen the registration window to start there instead:

```sh
pnpm exec clubspot-sync --club <id> --camp <camp-id> --since 2026-01-01 --dry-run
```

`--dry-run` is the way to check a backfill before committing to it: it logs the writes without
making them. `--since` only widens the registration read; the schedule pass (`programs`,
`sessions`, `classes`, `session_classes`, `entry_caps`) is already a full reconcile on every run, so
it needs no override.

A successful backfill still records its own `started_at` in `sync_program_runs`, same as any other
run, so the camp's watermark advances from there - it doesn't replay the backfilled window on the
next normal run.

## Shape of the code

Each collection's mapping is a pure plan function, and a thin executor writes the plan. That keeps
almost all of the logic testable with no Directus and no Parse:

- `camps.ts` - discovers the camps for a club.
- `backoff.ts` - decides whether a camp is due for a sync this run.
- `schedule.ts` - plans `programs`, `sessions`, `classes`, `session_classes`, `entry_caps`.
- `people.ts` / `person-sync.ts` - person matching and the `people`/`contacts`/`medical_profiles`
  plan and its executor.
- `registrations.ts` - plans `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `registration_billing`,
  `custom_field_definitions`, `custom_field_responses`.
- `sync-log.ts` - the `sync_runs`/`sync_program_runs` collections and the per-camp watermark.
- `sync-run.ts` - the run loop that ties the above together for one camp.
- `directus.ts` - the Directus REST client.
- `main.ts` - the CLI.

## Behaviors worth knowing before you change this

**A person reference is resolved once, at creation, and never re-resolved.** `registrations.person_id`
and `contacts.person_id` are set when that row is created and left alone on every later run. That is
what makes a manual merge durable: staff repoint the FK and delete the duplicate, and no later sync
undoes it. See `docs/crm-schema.md` for the merge procedure.

**The sync cancels rather than deletes**, except for `session_classes`. A `registration_entries` row
whose Clubspot join object vanished gets `status = cancelled`, not deleted. `session_classes` is a
pure join with no status field of its own, so a class a session no longer offers is removed outright.

## Backoff

Each run lists every non-archived camp for the club, then decides per camp whether it's due:

- A camp with no sync history, or whose last sync wrote something, is due every run.
- A sync that writes nothing doubles the camp's interval, up to a cap of one week. `skipped` rows
  (a run that found the camp not due) don't count either way - only an actual sync moves the
  backoff.
- A due camp gets a full reconcile, not a partial one, so there's nothing for the interval to miss:
  an entry-cap change (no pointer back to its camp) or a delete (nothing in `updatedAt` reveals one)
  is picked up the same as any other change, without needing to be detected first.
- **Registrations** are still filtered on `updatedAt` between the camp's watermark and the run
  start. The watermark is per camp: the `started_at` of that camp's most recent successful
  `sync_program_runs` row, or the epoch if there is none - so a camp coming back from a long
  backoff still gets registrations from the entire gap, not just since its last run.

## Fix

Two parts, and the second matters more than the first.

**Handle the data.** `sessions.start_date` and `end_date` are NOT NULL in `packages/crm/schema.yaml`,
so a dateless session cannot be stored as-is. Decide between skipping it with a warning and making
the columns nullable. Skipping cascades: `registration_entries.session_id` is NOT NULL too, so
entries pointing at a skipped session must also be skipped, and silently dropping registrations is
the failure mode #128's review already caught once with the unbounded `find()`. Whatever is chosen,
a skipped row must be counted and logged, not quietly discarded.

**Widen the SDK types.** `startDate` and `endDate` on `CampSessionAttributes` should be optional,
because they are. Leaving them required means the next consumer writes the same crash.

## Impact

Blocks syncing this camp, and any other with the same shape. The failure is contained — the camp is
logged `failed`, the run continues, and the dry run wrote nothing — so it is not dangerous, just
blocking.

Worth checking how many camps are affected before choosing the fix: if it is one bad test session,
skip-and-warn is clearly right; if it is widespread, nullable columns may be.

I have enough to triage all five. Here's the call, then I'll start.

## Triage

**1. Hourly sync — tier 2, not tier 1.** It looked like a one-line cron change, but it isn't. `backoff.ts:7` sets `BASE_INTERVAL_MS = 6h` and its docstring explicitly binds it to the scheduler cadence: *"the Cloud Scheduler trigger — a camp that just wrote something is due again on the very next run."* Change only the cron and you get hourly runs that mostly skip, because each camp still isn't due for 6 hours. So the change is cron + constant + two stale comments. The backoff tests are all written relative to `BASE_INTERVAL_MS`, so they survive. Quiet camps would then walk 1h→2h→4h→… to the same one-week cap.

**2. Run counters — tier 2.** Half-built already: `sync_runs` has `programs_checked` and `programs_synced` (`sync-log.ts:20-24`). Adding skipped and failed is two columns in `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, two fields on `FinishRunResult`, and counting in the `runSync` loop — which already tracks both (`status: "skipped"` at `sync-run.ts`, and `failedCampIds`).

**3. Directus admin — tier 3.** `DirectusRole` (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/resources.ts`) creates a policy with `app_access` but has no `admin_access` at all, so this adds a field to the shared resource class *and* changes the access model. CLAUDE.md is explicit that grants are deliberate and least-privilege, and there's a real choice: make Staff itself admin, add a separate Administrator role, or attach an admin policy to your account alone. Short design doc, not a long one.

**4. Failed syncs — blocked.** `gcloud logging read` failed: *"Reauthentication failed. cannot prompt during non-interactive execution."* I need you to run `! gcloud auth login`. Meanwhile #131 is the filed one (dateless camp session crashes `planSessions`), and the issue itself says the fix depends on data — skip-and-warn if it's one bad test session, nullable columns if it's widespread. So it needs the log/data answer before it can be dispatched.

**5. Directus UX options — answering below, no code.**

## Directus UX options (v12.3.1)

For "let staff clean up people data before it feeds email lists", in rough order of effort:

- **Nothing — just the Data Studio.** Collection layouts, saved presets, field grouping, conditional fields. A saved preset filtered to "people missing or with a bad email", with only the fields that matter visible, is a usable review queue and costs zero code. This is the honest first answer for a cleanup workflow.
- **Directus Insights panels.** Dashboards for the counts — dovetails with item 2 and with #123, which already proposes replacing the capacity worksheet with a panel.
- **Directus Flows.** No-code automation with a manual trigger button on a collection. Good for "mark reviewed", "merge these two", "push to list" as an operator action.
- **A custom Interface or Module extension.** Vue extensions loaded into the Data Studio. This is where a bespoke merge/dedupe screen would live if presets aren't enough. Real build-and-deploy cost, and the substrate runs a stock `directus/directus:12.3.1` image, so it'd need an extensions volume or a derived image.
- **A separate app.** Your own frontend against the Directus REST API, like `portal` is today. Most control, most work, and a second auth surface.

My read: start at preset-plus-Flow and only build an extension if that provably fails. But that's the tier-3 design conversation, and it's downstream of the email-list work — I'd rather scope it once you've seen the failed-sync data, since data quality is the thing the UX has to fix.

## Starting now

Nothing is running, so I'll take item 1. Two asks: run `! gcloud auth login` when convenient to unblock item 4, and tell me if you'd rather I reorder.

# Implement a Task

Hand one scoped change to a sub-agent. The sub-agent edits, verifies, and commits. You review the result.

The sub-agent starts cold. It knows nothing about the session, the previous tasks, or the conversation. Everything it needs goes in the brief.

## 1. Prepare the brief

Find the exact `path:line` anchors yourself before you write the brief. A brief that names a file and a line is worth far more than one that describes a symptom.

Use `Agent` with `subagent_type: implementer`.

The agent already knows the conventions, the test pattern, the `just` rules, and the git rules — they are in `.claude/agents/implementer.md`. Do not repeat them. The brief carries only what is specific to this task:

**Task.** What to change, concretely, with `path:line` anchors.

**Scope fence.** The exact boundary of this change. Name anything adjacent it must not touch.

**Context it cannot derive.** A decision already made, a constraint from the design doc, a reason the obvious approach is wrong. If an approved design doc covers this step, give its path and the step number.

**Never ask for a comment.** Give the agent the constraint and let the standing rule in `CLAUDE.md` decide whether it earns a comment. A brief that says "leave a comment explaining why" overrides that rule, and the agent will write five lines where none were needed.

**Acceptance.** How to know the change worked — the behavior that should differ, or the test that should now pass.

## 3. Review the result

1. Run `git show --stat HEAD`. Read the full diff if the change is non-trivial.
2. Check that the diff stayed inside the scope fence.
3. Summarize for the user in two or three lines: what changed, whether the checks passed, and anything the sub-agent flagged.

If the work is wrong or too wide, dispatch a follow-up sub-agent or run `git revert`. Do not patch it by hand — that defeats the point of delegating.

## Rules

This is worse than "a few failed syncs". Here's what the logs say.

## The sync has never successfully synced anything

Every run reports `programsChecked: 38, programsSynced: 0`. Across 380 failure events in 30 days, **all 38 camps fail**, in three distinct classes that partition the set exactly:

| Class | Camps | Events | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `registration_billing.currency` required — Directus 400 | 14 | 140 | **not filed** |
| `entry_cap` → unknown session (`requireLookup` throws) | 13 | 130 | **not filed** |
| Dateless session → `toISOString` on undefined | 11 | 110 | #131 |

14 + 13 + 11 = 38. Not one bad test session — the whole club.

**This also answers #131's open question.** The issue says *"if it is one bad test session, skip-and-warn is clearly right; if it is widespread, nullable columns may be."* It's widespread: 11 of 38 camps.

**All three are the same bug.** An SDK type declares a field required, live Clubspot data disagrees, and the CRM column is NOT NULL, so the row is rejected and the camp dies:

- `registrations.ts:228` — `currency: billing.get("currency")` is `undefined` for some billing objects.
- `schedule.ts:142` — an entry cap's `campSessionObject` points at a session excluded from `planSessions`. `main.ts:62` filters sessions with `.notEqualTo("archived", true)` but pulls entry caps from `campClass.get("entryCapsArray")` with no such filter, so a cap on an archived session has nothing to resolve against.
- `schedule.ts:31` — `toDateString` on a session with no `startDate`/`endDate`.

Fixing these one at a time would produce three inconsistent answers to one question: *what does the sync do when Clubspot data violates a CRM constraint — skip, null, or default?* So I'm treating item 4 as **tier 3** and sending it to `design` as a single decision, not three patches.

**One more thing the logs show, which argues for item 2.** The 19:00 run on 09-17 reported `status: "ok"` with `failedCampIds: []` — because all 38 camps were skipped by backoff, 4 minutes short of the 6-hour interval. A run where nothing succeeds and nothing is attempted currently looks healthy. `programs_skipped` would have made that obvious at a glance.

I haven't filed issues for the two unfiled bugs yet — if the design lands this session they'd close immediately. Say the word if you want them tracked regardless.

158 .claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md
# Handling Clubspot data the CRM schema rejects

## Context

`clubspot-sync` has never completed a camp in production. Every run since it was turned on reports
`programsChecked: 38, programsSynced: 0`; the 38 camps fail in three classes that partition the set
exactly (11 + 13 + 14).

The camps are not untouched. `applyPlan` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-run.ts:171`) writes each
collection to Directus as it is planned, and nothing wraps a camp in a transaction, so a camp that
throws has already committed everything upstream of the throw. `programsSynced` counts only camps
that finished every collection. So the CRM already holds programs for all 38, schedule rows for the
27 that got past `planSessions`, and people, registrations and registration entries for the 14 that
reached billing. The real failure mode is **one bad row leaves a camp half-written, and every run
re-walks the same path and dies in the same place** — hourly, since `campBackoff` deliberately does
not lengthen the interval after a failure (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:32-36`).

**Class A — dateless session (11 camps, #131).** `toDateString`
(`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:31`) dereferences `session.get("startDate")`, which is
`undefined` on live data. `CampSessionAttributes` declares both dates required
(`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:301-302`); `sessions.start_date` / `end_date` are
`is_nullable: false` (`packages/crm/schema.yaml:4145`, `:4185`).

**Class B — entry cap on an unresolvable session (13 camps, not filed).** `requireLookup`
(`schedule.ts:21-27`) throws from `planEntryCaps` (`schedule.ts:142`). Each affected camp names
exactly one session id and all 13 are distinct — one bad cap per camp, with any others hidden
behind the throw.

The coordinator's hypothesis is the archived filter: sessions are fetched with
`.notEqualTo("archived", true)` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:62`) while entry caps come off
`campClass.get("entryCapsArray")` unfiltered (`main.ts:66`). I could confirm the shape but not the
cause. The lookup map is built from the whole CRM `sessions` table, not just this camp's fetch
(`sync-run.ts:269`), so an unresolvable id means that session has **never** been in the CRM.
Archived before the sync ever ran, and deleted in Clubspot leaving a dangling pointer, both produce
exactly that. Telling them apart needs a live Clubspot query, which this session had no credentials
for. Both are permanent, so the handling is the same either way.

**Class C — missing billing currency (14 camps, not filed).** This one is not a bad-data problem at
all. `queryCampEntries` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts:9-22`) does not
`include("billing_registration")`, so `registration.get("billing_registration")`
(`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:210`) returns an **unfetched pointer**: every `get` on
it returns `undefined`. `centsOrZero` (`:201`) silently turns each amount into `0`, and `currency`
(`:228`) has no fallback, so Directus rejects the row. The zeros are the worse half of the bug — the
400 is the only reason the CRM does not already hold a table of fake zero billing. The sibling query
`queryRegistrations` includes it (`queries.ts:36`), as does the admin-functions report
(`packages/admin-functions/src/registrations.ts:66`).

## Approach

**Policy.** A missing scalar makes the column nullable. An unresolvable reference skips the row,
with a warning naming both ids. Never fabricate a value, and never drop a row silently.

**Class A — nullable.** `sessions.start_date` / `end_date` become nullable in
`packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `SessionRow` (`packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:11-18`) takes
`string | null`, `CampSessionAttributes` is corrected to optional, and `planSessions` writes null.
That is what the policy prefers anyway, and it dissolves the cascade #131 worried about: the session
row exists, so entry caps, `session_classes` and `registration_entries` still resolve against it and
no registration is dropped. A skip would have cost registration data to avoid an empty date column.

**Class B — skip, and it is not a nullability question.** `entry_caps.session_id` is already
nullable (`schema.yaml:1335`), but null there means "this cap applies across every session"
(`packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:36`), so writing null would invent a fact. `planEntryCaps` drops the
cap and warns. The same guard goes on `planRegistrationEntries` (`registrations.ts:179`), which has
the identical latent failure and where a skip is real data loss — its warning carries the
registration, session and join ids so a dropped entry is traceable.

**Class C — fix the fetch; the policy is only the residual guard.** Add
`include("billing_registration")` to `queryCampEntries`, and make `buildRegistrationBillingRow`
refuse an unfetched pointer rather than write zeros. Separately `currency` becomes nullable and
`BillingRegistrationAttributes.currency` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:147`) optional, since
a free registration may carry no currency even once fetched.

**SDK type corrections are in scope**, in the commit for the class that needs each one. Widening
`startDate`/`endDate` to optional breaks `planSessions`'s compile on its own, so splitting them into
a step of their own would land a commit that does not build.

**Partial writes stay.** Directus REST has no cross-collection transaction, so per-camp atomicity is
not reachable without more machinery than this justifies. Both passes are idempotent upserts keyed
on Clubspot ids, and person references are pinned at creation (`sync-run.ts:345-351`), so a
half-written camp converges on the next successful run rather than duplicating. What makes that
acceptable is the warning: without it, "converged" and "gave up on a row" look the same from
outside.

**Recovery needs no backfill.** `watermarkForCamp` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:12-17`)
reads the newest **`ok`** program run, and no camp has one, so every camp's watermark is still the
epoch. The first run after these fixes re-reads every registration from the beginning and reconciles
the full schedule, which closes the Class C hole — but only because it happens before any camp
records an `ok` run. Two consequences: no `--since` backfill is needed if these ship together, and
`registration_billing` should be empty today (every billing create carried `currency: undefined` and
failed), so there are no zeroed rows to clean up. Confirm that with one read before deploying rather
than assuming it.

**Deploy order.** `scripts/deploy:7-8` applies `infrastructure` (the job image) before `crm` (the
schema), so between them the new code can run against the old NOT NULL columns. That failure is the
same contained per-camp failure and self-heals the next hour. Both nullability changes drop NOT
NULL, the safe direction for a migration; adding it back later would fail against any null rows
written meanwhile.

## Alternatives

- **Skip dateless sessions instead of nulling the dates** — cascades into `registration_entries`,
  so it drops real registrations to avoid an empty column. #131 raised it as the likely answer; it
  is the wrong trade.
- **Drop the `archived` filter at `main.ts:62`** — a one-line fix for Class B *if* archiving is the
  cause, but `sessions` has no archived column (`docs/crm-schema.md:116`), so retired sessions would
  present as current, and dateless archived sessions would arrive too.
- **Represent archived sessions properly (an `archived` column on `sessions`)** — the correct
  long-term answer to Class B, and the only one that keeps a registration entry pointing at a
  since-archived session. A schema and mapping change well beyond this fix; capture it as an issue.
- **Default `currency` to `"usd"`** — the club only transacts in USD, but it fabricates a value in a
  financial table, and it would have masked the unfetched-pointer bug completely.
- **Make a camp atomic** — no cross-collection transaction in Directus REST, and a
  compensating-delete implementation would be more dangerous than the partial writes it replaces.

## Open questions

1. **Class B's root cause is unconfirmed** — archived session, or deleted session with a dangling
   cap pointer. The skip handles both, and its warning will identify which on the next run. If you
   want to know first, it needs one live Clubspot query with credentials I did not have.
2. **Should archived sessions be represented in the CRM** (an `archived` column on `sessions`)
   rather than skipped? That is a different, larger design. Capture as an issue, or fold in now?
3. **Where should skip counts live?** This design logs them (`winston.warn`, the precedent at
   `registrations.ts:52-63`) and adds no counter, so it touches neither `sync-log.ts` nor
   `sync-run.ts`. A durable count means an `items_skipped` column on `sync_program_runs`, which
   overlaps the queued task adding `programs_skipped` / `programs_failed` to `sync_runs` — it should
   ride with that work, not this.
4. **If a fetched billing object still has no currency, is null acceptable in reports**, or does
   finance need a value there?

## Steps

1. **Fetch billing properly.** Add `include("billing_registration")` to `queryCampEntries`
   (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts`), and make `buildRegistrationBillingRow` throw on a
   billing pointer whose data was never fetched instead of writing zeros. Verify: cases in
   `packages/clubspot-sync/test/registrations.test.ts` for a fetched object and an unfetched
   pointer, using the fake-Parse-object pattern at
   `packages/clubspot-sync/test/schedule.test.ts:14-16`.
2. **Nullable session dates (Class A, #131).** `CampSessionAttributes.startDate`/`endDate` optional;
   `sessions.start_date`/`end_date` nullable and `required: false` in `packages/crm/schema.yaml`;
   `SessionRow` takes `string | null`; `planSessions` writes null and warns once per dateless
   session. Verify: unit test on `planSessions`, plus `just directus-local` to confirm the applied
   schema accepts a null date.
3. **Skip unresolvable session references (Class B).** `planEntryCaps` and `planRegistrationEntries`
   drop a row whose session id is not in the lookup map, warning with the owning ids, instead of
   throwing. `requireLookup` stays as it is for program and class references, which are not
   optional. Verify: unit tests for both plan functions asserting the row is absent and the rest of
   the plan is unaffected.
4. **Nullable billing currency (Class C residual).** `BillingRegistrationAttributes.currency`
   optional, `registration_billing.currency` nullable and `required: false`,
   `RegistrationBillingRow.currency` takes `string | null`, mapping passes null through. Verify:
   unit test, plus `just directus-local`.
5. **Write the policy down.** One paragraph in `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` under "Behaviors
   worth knowing before you change this", and the nullability notes in `docs/crm-schema.md` for the
   three columns. Close #131.

After the deploy, verification is one run: `programsSynced` should reach 38, and any remaining
`Camp sync failed` names a class not covered here. Before it, `--camp <id> --dry-run` against one
camp from each class is the cheap check.

## Design doc ready for approval

**`.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md`** (158 lines)

**Summary in three lines.** One policy: a missing scalar makes the column nullable, an unresolvable reference skips the row with a warning naming both ids, nothing is fabricated and nothing is dropped silently. Class A gets nullable session dates — which dissolves the registration cascade #131 feared. Class B skips the cap, and the same latent guard goes on `planRegistrationEntries`. Class C turns out not to fit the policy at all.

**The finding that matters more than the three bugs.** Class C is not bad data — it's a fetch bug. `queryCampEntries` never includes `billing_registration`, so the pointer is unfetched and *every* `get` on it returns `undefined`. `centsOrZero` (`registrations.ts:201`) silently converts all twelve amounts to `0`. Only `currency` lacks a fallback. **The 400 error is the only thing that has kept a table of fake zero billing out of the CRM.** Had currency been nullable from the start, you'd have 14 camps of financial data reading zero and no error anywhere.

That reframes the whole item: the crash was load-bearing.

**My answers to its four open questions**, so you're not handed homework:

1. **Class B root cause** — don't block on it. Archived-session and dangling-pointer both produce identical symptoms and identical handling; the skip warning will name which on the next run. I can probe Clubspot directly if you want certainty first, but I'd ship without it.
2. **Archived sessions as a first-class CRM concept** — capture as an issue, don't fold in. It's a real schema design and the skip is safe meanwhile.
3. **Skip counts** — agreed, they ride with the queued counters task. That grows item 2 slightly: `items_skipped` on `sync_program_runs` alongside `programs_skipped`/`programs_failed` on `sync_runs`. Better than two half-measures.
4. **Null currency in reports** — null is fine. I grepped: nothing consumes the column. Defaulting to `"usd"` is what would have hidden the zeros bug, so I'd keep refusing to fabricate it.

**Two caveats the doc raises and I'd act on.** `registration_billing` should be empty right now — worth one read before deploying rather than assuming. And `scripts/deploy:7-8` applies the job image before the schema, so there's a one-hour window where new code meets old NOT NULL columns; contained and self-healing, but you'll see failures in that gap.

**Do you approve?** On approval I'll commit the doc and run its 5 steps in order, starting with step 1 — which is the one that stops the zeros.
I can confirm registration_billing is empty. Don't capture archived sessions as a separate issue, just do it.

Noted on `registration_billing` — that removes the pre-deploy check.

Folding archived sessions in is a real design change, not a step, so I'm sending the doc back rather than improvising it. One dependency you should know about, because it decides whether the work pays off:

**Representing archived sessions only fixes Class B if archiving is actually the cause.** The doc established that an unresolvable session id means that session has *never* been in the CRM, and two things produce that: it was archived before the sync first ran, or it was deleted in Clubspot leaving a dangling cap pointer. If it's the second, an `archived` column changes nothing and the skip is still what saves those 13 camps. So we'll need both regardless — the archived column as the correct representation, the skip as the guard for genuinely dangling pointers.

Confirming which needs one live Clubspot query, which the designer was denied credentials for. If you want certainty before we build, run `! gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=clubspot-username` (and `clubspot-password`) — or just tell me if you already know whether those 13 sessions are archived rather than deleted. Either way I'll proceed; it changes emphasis, not direction.

Two decisions from the user. Revise the doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md` in place.

**1. Open question 2 is answered: fold it in.** The user said, verbatim: "Don't capture archived sessions as a separate issue, just do it." So archived sessions become first-class in the CRM as part of this design, not a follow-up issue. Update the Approach, Alternatives (it currently lists this as a rejected alternative — it is now the chosen one), Open questions, and Steps accordingly.

**2. Open question from the pre-deploy checks is closed.** The user confirms `registration_billing` is empty in the live CRM. Drop that verification step; your reasoning about no zeroed rows to clean up holds.

## What folding it in has to cover

Design it properly rather than bolting a column on:

- An `archived` column on `sessions` in `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `SessionRow`, and the `planSessions` mapping, sourced from the Clubspot `CampSession.archived` attribute.
- `main.ts:62` currently fetches sessions with `.notEqualTo("archived", true)`. That filter goes away, since the point is to represent archived sessions rather than hide them. Say what that implies: more sessions arrive, some of which may be dateless — which your Class A fix already covers, so check that the two compose and state it.
- What `archived` means downstream. A registration entry pointing at a since-archived session must keep resolving — that was your own argument for why this is the correct long-term answer. Confirm it holds.
- Whether archived sessions should be hidden by default in the Directus UI (a filter or a layout default) rather than only stored, since the user is about to start navigating this data by hand. Keep this brief — it borders on a separate UX task already queued — but note it if the schema should carry anything for it.

## What does NOT change

**Keep the Class B skip.** Representing archived sessions only resolves caps whose session was archived. A cap whose session was *deleted* in Clubspot leaves a dangling pointer that no column fixes, and you established both produce identical symptoms. So the skip in `planEntryCaps` and the new guard on `planRegistrationEntries` both stay, as the guard for the genuinely unresolvable case. Make that layering explicit in the doc: archived column first (correct representation), skip second (last-resort guard). Do not let the skip quietly disappear because the column is expected to handle most cases.

Your open question 1 (archived vs deleted) therefore stays open and gets *more* important, since it now determines how much of Class B the new column actually fixes. Keep it, and sharpen it: say what we would expect to see on the first run after this ships under each hypothesis, so the warning output tells us the answer without a separate probe.

## Constraints

- Steps must stay ordered, separable, and independently verifiable — I dispatch one `implement` sub-agent per step. Adding the archived work will likely add a step; put it where the dependencies require rather than appending it.
- Note the migration implication of the new column the way you did for the nullability changes (adding a column is the safe direction; say whether it needs a backfill for existing `sessions` rows).
- Everything else in the doc stands. Do not rewrite what is already settled — Class A nullable dates, Class C's fetch fix and the unfetched-pointer refusal, partial writes, recovery needing no backfill, skip counts riding with the queued counters task.

# Capture an Issue

Turn a problem — from the current conversation or the user's description — into a well-formed GitHub issue in `cyc-seattle/isthmia`.

## When to file one

File an issue when the work will outlive the current session: a problem found mid-task that you
are deliberately not fixing now, a known defect with no owner, or work that needs to be scheduled.

Do **not** file an issue for work you are about to do in this session. The session's pull request
records it. See the Workflow section of `CLAUDE.md`.

## Steps

1. **Gather the problem.** Pull details from the conversation or ask the user. A good issue needs: what's wrong or wanted, where in the code (`path:line`), and why it matters.
2. **Check for duplicates first.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels`. If it overlaps an existing issue, tell the user and offer to comment on / rescope that one instead of filing a new duplicate.
3. **Pick a type label:** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, or `docker`.
4. **Assign a priority label** using the rubric below.
5. **Write the body** using the template below. Reference concrete files as `path:line`.
6. **Create it:** `gh issue create --title "<imperative title>" --label "<type>,<priority>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`
7. **Report** the issue number and URL back to the user.

## Priority rubric (P0–P3)

- **P0 — Critical:** data integrity/corruption, production broken, or a security-critical hole. Work starts immediately.
- **P1 — High:** a significant bug or friction the user hits regularly, with no safe workaround (e.g. auth/tooling breakage).
- **P2 — Medium:** a real improvement or a bug with a workaround (added tests, hardening, moderate bugs).
- **P3 — Low:** cleanup, docs, polish, low-risk nice-to-haves.

## Body template

Keep it tight. Use `## Problem` always; then `## Fix` (bugs) or `## Proposed changes` / `## Scope` (enhancements); add `## Impact` when the "why" isn't obvious.

```markdown
## Problem

<what's wrong/wanted, with `path:line` references and a code snippet if useful>

## Fix

<concrete change; mention adding a regression test for bugs>

## Impact

<why it matters — omit if self-evident>
```

## Conventions

- **Title:** short, imperative, no priority prefix (priority lives in the label). e.g. "safeCall retries non-retryable errors with a 60s delay".
- Labels already exist: `P0`–`P3`, `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `docker`. Don't invent new ones without asking.
- For bugs, always note that the fix should include a regression test — tests live in `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`.
- Cross-link related issues with `#N` and note dependencies ("land #47 first").

## Problem

Before people data can feed email lists (#71), staff need a way to review and correct it. The
built-in Data Studio layouts are not adequate for this: relational fields render the related row's
UUID rather than anything human-readable, so navigating from a person to their `contact_links` shows
a list of ids.

The UUID symptom specifically is *not* what this issue is about — every collection in
`packages/crm/schema.yaml` has `display_template: null`, and setting those is a separate, much
cheaper fix being done now. This issue covers what remains once labels are readable: a purpose-built
review and cleanup surface.

## Scope

A Directus Interface or Module extension for the people-data cleanup workflow. Exact features should
be decided after the display templates land and the data can actually be browsed — the list below is
the expected shape, not a commitment:

- Reviewing people with missing, malformed, or duplicate email addresses.

## Approach

**Policy.** A missing scalar makes the column nullable. An unresolvable reference skips the row,
with a warning naming both ids. Never fabricate a value, and never drop a row silently.

**Class A — nullable.** `sessions.start_date` / `end_date` become nullable in
`packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `SessionRow` (`packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:11-18`) takes
`string | null`, `CampSessionAttributes` is corrected to optional, and `planSessions` writes null.
That is what the policy prefers anyway, and it dissolves the cascade #131 worried about: the session
row exists, so entry caps, `session_classes` and `registration_entries` still resolve against it and
no registration is dropped. A skip would have cost registration data to avoid an empty date column.

**Class B — two layers: represent archived sessions, then skip what is still unresolvable.**

*Layer one, the correct representation.* `sessions` gains an `archived` boolean, mapped from
`CampSession.archived`, and the filter at `main.ts:62` goes away so archived sessions are synced
like any other. The SDK already types the attribute — `CampSessionAttributes` extends
`ClubspotAttributes` extends `ArchiveAttributes` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:4-8`) — so no
type correction is needed here. The column mirrors `registrations.archived` exactly
(`packages/crm/schema.yaml:3862-3899`): `default_value: false`, `is_nullable: false`. That default
is also the migration: existing `sessions` rows were all written under the old filter, so every one
of them is genuinely unarchived and the default backfills them correctly. No manual backfill.

Two consequences to check when implementing. More sessions now arrive, some of which may be
dateless — which is exactly what Class A's nullable dates already handle, so the two compose and
neither needs to know about the other; sequencing Class A first is what makes that true.
`planSessionClasses` (`schedule.ts:162`) also expands over every fetched session, so archived
sessions get their `session_classes` rows too. That is consistent — the session is represented, and
so is what it offered — and the join carries no independent meaning to go stale.

Downstream, a registration entry pointing at a since-archived session now resolves instead of
being dropped. That was the argument for doing this at all, and it holds: `planRegistrationEntries`
(`registrations.ts:179`) looks the session up in the same map, which is built from the CRM
`sessions` table.

For the Data Studio, the `sessions` collection meta already carries Directus's archive keys unset —
`archive_field: null`, `archive_value: null`, `unarchive_value: null`, `archive_app_filter: true`
(`packages/crm/schema.yaml:359-380`). Pointing `archive_field` at the new column, with
`archive_value: "true"` / `unarchive_value: "false"`, hides archived sessions from the app's default
list view for free. That is the whole of the UI concern here; anything beyond it belongs to the
queued UX work. One thing to verify rather than assume: the sync's own reads
(`readItems("sessions", { limit: -1 })`, `sync-run.ts:138`) must keep returning archived rows, or
reconciliation would create duplicates of every archived session on the next run.

*Layer two, the last-resort guard.* The column only rescues caps whose session was archived. A cap
whose session was **deleted** in Clubspot points at nothing any column can hold, so `planEntryCaps`
still drops that row and warns. `entry_caps.session_id` is nullable (`schema.yaml:1335`), but null
there means "this cap applies across every session" (`packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:36`), so writing
null would invent a fact. The same guard goes on `planRegistrationEntries`, which has the identical
latent failure and where a skip is real data loss — its warning carries the registration, session
and join ids so a dropped entry is traceable. The guard stays regardless of how much of Class B the
archived column turns out to fix.

**Class C — fix the fetch; the policy is only the residual guard.** Add
`include("billing_registration")` to `queryCampEntries`, and make `buildRegistrationBillingRow`
refuse an unfetched pointer rather than write zeros. Separately `currency` becomes nullable and
`BillingRegistrationAttributes.currency` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:147`) optional, since
a free registration may carry no currency even once fetched.

**SDK type corrections are in scope**, in the commit for the class that needs each one. Widening
`startDate`/`endDate` to optional breaks `planSessions`'s compile on its own, so splitting them into
a step of their own would land a commit that does not build.

**Partial writes stay.** Directus REST has no cross-collection transaction, so per-camp atomicity is
not reachable without more machinery than this justifies. Both passes are idempotent upserts keyed
on Clubspot ids, and person references are pinned at creation (`sync-run.ts:345-351`), so a
half-written camp converges on the next successful run rather than duplicating. What makes that
acceptable is the warning: without it, "converged" and "gave up on a row" look the same from
outside.

**Recovery needs no backfill.** `watermarkForCamp` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:12-17`)
reads the newest **`ok`** program run, and no camp has one, so every camp's watermark is still the
epoch. The first run after these fixes re-reads every registration from the beginning and reconciles
the full schedule, which closes the Class C hole — but only because it happens before any camp
records an `ok` run. So no `--since` backfill is needed if these ship together.

**Deploy order.** `scripts/deploy:7-8` applies `infrastructure` (the job image) before `crm` (the
schema), so between them the new code can run against the old columns. That failure is the same
contained per-camp failure and self-heals the next hour. Dropping NOT NULL and adding a column with
a default are both the safe direction; re-adding NOT NULL later would fail against any null rows
written meanwhile.

Step 1 of an approved design: fix the billing fetch so `clubspot-sync` stops silently writing zeros for every financial field.

Working tree: /Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync (branch session/people-sync). Work only there.

Design doc: `.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md`. Read its Context and the Class C parts of Approach before you start. You are implementing **Step 1 only**.

## The bug

`queryCampEntries` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts:9-22`) includes `classes`, `sessions`, `sessionJoinObjects.*` and `participantsArray`, but **not** `billing_registration`. So `registration.get("billing_registration")` in `buildRegistrationBillingRow` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:210`) returns an *unfetched Parse pointer*: the object exists and is truthy, but every `get` on it returns `undefined`.

`centsOrZero` (`registrations.ts:201`) then turns all twelve amount fields into `0`. Only `currency` (`:228`) has no fallback, so Directus rejects the row with a 400 and the camp dies. That 400 is currently the only thing keeping a table of fake zero billing out of the CRM — 14 of 38 camps fail here.

The sibling query `queryRegistrations` (`queries.ts:36`) already includes `billing_registration`, as does `packages/admin-functions/src/registrations.ts:66`.

## Task

Two changes.

**1. Add `include("billing_registration")` to `queryCampEntries`.**

**2. Make `buildRegistrationBillingRow` refuse an unfetched pointer** instead of writing zeros. It currently returns `undefined` when `billing_registration` is absent, which is correct and must stay — a registration with no billing legitimately produces no row. What it must not do is proceed when the pointer is present but its data was never fetched. Throwing is what the design specifies: the camp fails loudly rather than writing twelve wrong numbers, and a thrown camp is already contained by the run loop.

Use Parse's own notion of whether an object's data is loaded rather than probing individual fields — an object whose data is fetched can still legitimately have an undefined `currency`, and step 5 of this design makes exactly that case nullable, so the two must not be conflated.

## Scope fence

Touch only `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts`, `packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts`, and `packages/clubspot-sync/test/registrations.test.ts`.

Do not touch:
- `centsOrZero`'s behavior for a genuinely fetched object whose individual amount is absent. Zero is right there.
- `currency` nullability, `RegistrationBillingRow`, or `packages/crm/schema.yaml`. That is step 5 — leave the 400 in place for the unfetched case, which this step makes unreachable.
- `planSessions`, `planEntryCaps`, `planRegistrationEntries`, or anything about session dates or archived sessions. Those are steps 2, 3 and 4.
- `sync-log.ts`, `sync-run.ts`, or any counter.

## Context you cannot derive

- The existing tests at `packages/clubspot-sync/test/registrations.test.ts:251-334` all build billing as a *fetched* fake object with `currency: "usd"`, which is precisely why this bug was never caught. Do not delete them; add the unfetched case alongside.
- The fake-Parse-object pattern to follow is at `packages/clubspot-sync/test/schedule.test.ts:14-16`.
- `packages/clubspot-sdk` is a separate package from `packages/clubspot-sync`; a change to the former needs the workspace build to pick it up. `just build` or `just ci` handles that.

## Acceptance

- `just check` and `just test` pass.
- A new test proves `buildRegistrationBillingRow` throws (not returns zeros) for a billing pointer whose data was never fetched.
- A new or existing test proves a registration with no `billing_registration` at all still returns `undefined`, unchanged.
- The existing fetched-object tests still pass untouched.

One commit.

Working tree: /Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync (branch session/people-sync). Work only there.

Design doc: `.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md`. Read its Context and the Class A part of Approach. You are implementing **Step 2 only**. Steps 1 (billing fetch) is already committed; steps 3-6 are not yours.

This also closes the code side of issue #131 — read that issue, it has analysis worth having. Do not close the issue itself; step 6 does that.

## The bug

`toDateString` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:31`) calls `.toISOString()` on `session.get("startDate")`, which is `undefined` on live data:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toISOString')
    at toDateString (schedule.ts:31)
    at planSessions
```

11 of 38 camps die here every run. `CampSessionAttributes` declares `startDate: Date` and `endDate: Date` as required (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:301-302`); live data disagrees.

## Task

Make a dateless session sync as a row with null dates, rather than crashing or being skipped.

- `CampSessionAttributes.startDate` / `endDate` become optional in `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`.
- `sessions.start_date` and `sessions.end_date` become nullable in `packages/crm/schema.yaml` — `is_nullable: true` on the field, and `required: false` in its meta. They are around lines 4145 and 4185; confirm rather than trusting those numbers.
- `SessionRow` (`packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:11-18`) takes `string | null` for both.
- `planSessions` writes null instead of throwing, and warns once per dateless session, naming the Clubspot session id so it is traceable.

## Why nullable and not skip

#131 proposed skipping the session, and the design rejected that deliberately. `registration_entries.session_id` is NOT NULL, so skipping a session cascades into dropping real registrations. Keeping the row with null dates means entry caps, `session_classes` and `registration_entries` all still resolve against it and no registration is lost. Do not implement a skip.

## Scope fence

Touch only: `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`, `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts`, `packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts`, and the corresponding tests.

Do not touch:
- `main.ts`'s session query, the `archived` filter, or anything about archived sessions. That is step 3, and it depends on this step landing first.
- `planEntryCaps`, `planRegistrationEntries`, or `requireLookup`. That is step 4.
- `currency`, `registration_billing`, or `RegistrationBillingRow`. That is step 5.
- `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` or `docs/crm-schema.md`. That is step 6.
- Any other NOT NULL column in `schema.yaml`. Only these two.

## Context you cannot derive

- Widening the SDK types will break `planSessions`'s compile until you handle the undefined case — that is expected and is why the design keeps the type correction in this step rather than splitting it out. A commit that does not build is not acceptable.
- `packages/crm/schema.yaml` is large. Grep for the field definitions rather than reading it whole, and match the surrounding style exactly — look at how an already-nullable column in the same collection is expressed.
- Changing `schema.yaml` means a migration against the live Directus on the next deploy. Dropping NOT NULL is the safe direction, so no data migration is needed.
- The warning precedent to follow is `winston.warn` as used at `packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:52-63`.

## Acceptance

- `just check` and `just test` pass.
- A unit test proves `planSessions` produces a row with null dates for a session missing `startDate`, `endDate`, or both — and that the rest of the plan is unaffected.
- The existing `planSessions` tests still pass.
- `just directus-local` applies the schema and accepts a session row with a null `start_date`. If that command cannot be run in your environment, say so explicitly in your report rather than claiming it passed.

One commit.

**I did not commit anything.** I made the full set of changes described in the brief, confirmed they break the build in files outside the scope fence, then reverted everything back to a clean working tree.

### What I found

Widening `CampSessionAttributes.startDate`/`endDate` to optional (as the brief requires) breaks `tsc --build` in two files that the scope fence explicitly excludes from this change:

- `packages/admin-functions/src/roster.ts:419` — `DateTime.fromJSDate(session.get("startDate"), { zone: "utc" })`. `fromJSDate` requires a `Date`, not `Date | undefined`.
- `packages/todo-manager/src/main.ts:75-76` — `DateTime.fromJSDate(campSession.get("startDate"))` and the matching `endDate` line, same problem.

I confirmed this with a clean build (`just clean` then `just build`, and isolated `pnpm run build` in each package):

```
packages/admin-functions: src/roster.ts(419,46): error TS2345: Argument of type 'Date | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Date'.
packages/todo-manager: src/main.ts(75,45) and (76,43): same error, on startDate and endDate.
```

Other `CampSession.get("startDate"/"endDate")` call sites (`admin-functions/participants.ts`, `contacts.ts`, `sessions.ts`) go through `formatDate(date?: Date, ...)`, which already accepts `undefined`, so those are unaffected.

### Why I stopped instead of fixing it

The brief's scope fence says "Touch only: `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`, `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts`, `packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts`, and the corresponding tests" and separately lists things not to touch. `roster.ts` and `todo-manager/main.ts` are in neither package on that list, and the brief anticipated only `planSessions`'s compile breaking ("Widening the SDK types will break `planSessions`'s compile until you handle the undefined case"), not these two.

Fixing them isn't mechanical narration either — it's a real design question the brief doesn't answer: should a roster/email-scheduling job for a dateless session throw a clear error (since the whole point of those tools is to compute dates), fall back to some default, or skip the session? That's not mine to decide unilaterally, and doing it silently would widen the diff into two more packages the design doc's Step 2 never mentions.

This is exactly the design doc's Class A rationale running into a consumer the design doc didn't audit: `#131`/the design doc discuss `planSessions` and the CRM schema but never look at `roster.ts` or `todo-manager`, both of which also call `CampSession.get("startDate")` and assume it's present.

### What I verified before reverting

All the changes described in the brief were correct in isolation and matched the acceptance criteria:
- `CampSessionAttributes.startDate`/`endDate` → optional in `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`.
- `sessions.start_date`/`end_date` → `is_nullable: true`, `required: false` in `packages/crm/schema.yaml` (confirmed at lines 4145/4185 as the brief guessed, matching the style of the already-nullable `clubspot_session_id` field nearby).
- `SessionRow.start_date`/`end_date` → `string | null` in `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts`.
- `planSessions` in `packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts` writes null via a null-safe `toDateString`, and `winston.warn`s once per dateless session naming the Clubspot session id, following the `registrations.ts:52-63` precedent.
- Added tests to `packages/clubspot-sync/test/schedule.test.ts` covering both-dates-missing and one-date-missing, asserting the created row and the warning, alongside the existing passing tests.

I did not run `just directus-local` since the schema-only piece was never separately verifiable without the rest landing, and the build failure blocked full verification anyway.

### Recommendation

Someone with authority to widen the design needs to decide the fallback behavior for `roster.ts` and `todo-manager/main.ts` when a session lacks dates (e.g., a clear thrown error naming the session, since silently proceeding with a garbage date is worse than failing loudly) — then either fold that into Step 2's scope or add a follow-up step/issue for it before this ships, since Step 2 cannot land as scoped without breaking the build.</result>

Two facts that change what your instruction implies — worth stating before I revise anything.

**Archived *programs* are already filtered.** `discoverCamps` (`camps.ts:11`) does `.equalTo("archived", false)` on `Camp`. So the regular sync has never considered archived camps; all 38 are live ones. That part of what you want is already the behavior.

My reading of your instruction: both filters stay in scheduled runs, a CLI flag opts into archived data for manual backfill, `sessions.archived` still becomes a column so backfilled archived sessions are represented honestly, and the skip guard becomes the primary Class B handler rather than a last resort. Proceeding on that unless you say otherwise.

On the 2024 dates — good, that's the better fix. I'd still keep nullable dates as hardening rather than the mechanism: the code shouldn't crash on data you haven't gotten to yet, and it shouldn't re-break the moment another legacy record turns up.

input.prompt:
Step 3 of an approved design: stop an entry cap pointing at an unknown session from killing its whole camp.

Working tree: /Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync (branch session/people-sync). Work only there.

Design doc: `.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md`. Read its Context and the Class B part of Approach. You are implementing **Step 3 only**. Steps 1 and 2 landed (`2a416f10`, `5ec4a169`); steps 4-6 are not yours.

## The bug

`requireLookup` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:22`) throws when a Clubspot id has no CRM row:

```
Error: No CRM session row for Clubspot id <id>; sync sessions before this collection
```

`planEntryCaps` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:140`) hits this for 13 of 38 camps, every run. Sessions are fetched with `.notEqualTo("archived", true)` (`main.ts:62`) while entry caps come off `campClass.get("entryCapsArray")` unfiltered, so a cap whose `campSessionObject` was archived — or deleted in Clubspot — has nothing to resolve against. That filter stays (step 4 adds a CLI flag to lift it for manual backfills), so this skip is the primary handler, not a fallback.

## Task

**`planEntryCaps`** — drop a cap whose session id is not in `sessionCrmIdByClubspotSessionId`, and warn naming both the entry cap id and the unresolved Clubspot session id. Do not write `null` for `session_id`: the column is nullable, but null there means "this cap applies across every session" (`packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:36`), so null would invent a fact.

**`planRegistrationEntries`** (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:164`) — the same latent failure on its `session_id` lookup. Drop the entry and warn, carrying the registration id, the unresolved session id, and the join object id, so a dropped entry is traceable. A skip here is real data loss, so the warning must be specific enough to find the row later.

`requireLookup` itself stays exactly as it is, and keeps throwing for **program** and **class** references. Those are not optional — a cap or entry with no resolvable class is a different bug, and silently dropping it would hide it.

## The trap in planRegistrationEntries

Read this before you edit it. That function does two things: it builds `desired` from `joinObjects`, and it separately builds `desiredKeys` from `joinObjects` to cancel existing entries whose join object has vanished:

```ts
const desiredKeys = new Set(joinObjects.map((joinObject) => joinObject.id));
for (const row of existingForRegistration) {
  if (row.id && row.status !== "cancelled" && !desiredKeys.has(row.clubspot_session_join_id)) {
    plan.toUpdate.push({ id: row.id, patch: { status: "cancelled" } });
  }
}
```

`desiredKeys` must keep being built from **all** `joinObjects`, including the ones you skip. If a skipped join object also drops out of `desiredKeys`, an existing entry row for it gets **cancelled** rather than left alone — silently marking a real registration cancelled because we could not resolve its session. That is worse than the crash this step replaces. A skipped row must be absent from `toCreate` and absent from `toUpdate`, leaving any existing row untouched.

Give every CRM collection a Directus `display_template` so related rows render as readable labels instead of UUIDs.

It is editing `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/start-session/SKILL.md`, and `.claude/skills/implement/SKILL.md`. Do not touch those.

## The problem

The user cannot navigate the CRM in the Directus Data Studio. Their words: "each person has contact_links, but these display as the ID of that collection, which is a UUID - not user friendly."

Cause: all 16 collections in `packages/crm/schema.yaml` have `display_template: null`. Directus renders a related item using the **related collection's** `display_template`, and with none set it falls back to the primary key. `people.contact_links` is an o2m alias over `contacts.person_id`, so it renders `contacts` rows — and `contacts` has no template, hence UUIDs.

## Task

Set a `display_template` on the collection `meta` of each of the 16 collections: `classes`, `contacts`, `custom_field_definitions`, `custom_field_responses`, `entry_caps`, `event_staff`, `medical_profiles`, `people`, `programs`, `registration_billing`, `registration_entries`, `registrations`, `session_classes`, `sessions`, `sync_program_runs`, `sync_runs`.

The syntax is Directus's mustache-style field interpolation, e.g. `{{first_name}} {{last_name}}`. Related fields can be traversed one level, e.g. `{{person_id.first_name}}`, which is the right answer for join and child collections that have no identifying field of their own.

Rules for choosing each template:

- **Read the collection's actual fields in `schema.yaml` first.** Do not guess field names or invent fields. A template referencing a non-existent field renders empty, which is worse than the UUID because it looks like missing data.
- **Prefer fields that cannot be null**, so a row never renders blank. Note that `sessions.start_date`/`end_date` and `registration_billing.currency` are now nullable (this branch made them so), so do not build a template that depends solely on those.
- Keep them short — a label, not a summary. Two or three fields at most.
- For a pure join like `session_classes`, traverse to both sides.
- For the log collections `sync_runs` and `sync_program_runs`, something time-based plus status is more useful than an id.

`docs/crm-schema.md` documents this data model. Update it only if it already records display templates or collection meta; if it does not, leave it alone and say so.

Touch only `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, and `docs/crm-schema.md` only under the condition above.

Do not touch:
- Any field definition, `is_nullable`, `required`, type, or relation. **Collection `meta.display_template` only.**
- `archive_field`, `archive_value`, `unarchive_value` on `sessions` — set deliberately earlier on this branch.
- Any `field`-level `display` or `display_options`. The collection-level template is the general fix; per-field overrides are out of scope.
- Any file under `packages/clubspot-sync/`, `packages/infrastructure/`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `.claude/`.

- Do not run `just build` or `just test` — they would race the other agent and fail for unrelated reasons. This is a YAML data change with no TypeScript impact. `just check` is expected (treefmt formats YAML); run it and report the result.
- A `display_template` change is metadata only. It needs no data migration and cannot fail against existing rows.
- `just directus-local` applies the schema locally. Use it if you want to confirm the templates are accepted, but it is not required — say either way what you did.
- `packages/crm/schema.yaml` is large. Grep for `display_template: null` to find all 16 sites, and read each collection's fields before editing its template.

## Problem

`registration_billing`'s collection `display_template` in `packages/crm/schema.yaml` is
`{{amount}} {{currency}}`. `amount` is integer cents, so a $120 registration renders as
`12000 usd` wherever Directus shows a related billing row.

The field's own `display_options` already format it as a currency in a normal column view, but a
`display_template` bypasses that and prints the raw stored value.

## Fix

Options, roughly in order of effort:

- Drop `{{amount}}` from the template and label the row some other way, letting the field's own
  currency formatting do the work in column views.
- Traverse to something human-readable instead. Note Directus only traverses one level from the
  collection, so `{{registration_id.person_id.first_name}}` will not work — `registration_id`
  alone would render using `registrations`' own template.
- Store a formatted display field, which is almost certainly not worth it.

## Impact

Cosmetic. `registration_billing` is a leaf table that is rarely shown as a related label, which is
why this was left as it shipped. Filed so it is not forgotten if someone starts building billing
views.

Context: the display templates were added across all 16 collections to fix relational fields
rendering UUIDs.
EOF

`custom_field_definitions`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `registration_billing`,
`custom_field_responses`.

The scheduled job moved from every six hours to hourly, so this went from 4 full reads a day of
each collection to 24.

This is deliberate and documented — the schedule pass is a full reconcile on every run, and the
plan functions resolve foreign keys against the whole CRM table rather than the current fetch,
which is what makes a manual backfill durable. So the reads are not accidental. They just do not
scale with the data.

## Proposed changes

Nothing is urgent at current volume — 38 camps, and `registration_billing` is only now starting to
fill. Worth revisiting when `registrations` or `registration_entries` grows past a few thousand

- Read only the fields each plan function actually needs, rather than whole rows.
- Scope the reads that can be scoped to the camp being synced, keeping full reads only where
  cross-camp resolution is genuinely required (`sessions`, for the backfill behavior above).
- Cache across camps within a run — already done via the `SharedTables` fold — and reconsider
  whether every collection needs re-reading on every run at all.

Measure before changing anything: the run currently finishes in a few seconds, so this is a
scaling concern, not a present problem.

# End a Session

Turn the session branch into one pull request. The human merges it, and that merge is the approval.

## 1. Check the tree

Run `git status --short`. The tree must be clean.

If work is uncommitted, ask the user whether to commit it or drop it. Do not open a PR over a dirty tree.

## 2. Run the full gate

```sh
just ci
```

This runs install, build, check, and test — the same gate as the GitHub Actions `pr.yml` workflow.

If it fails, fix it through `implement` so the fix gets its own commit. Do not open a PR on a red gate unless the user tells you to.

## 3. Review the diff

Run the `review` skill. Report the findings to the user.

The user decides what to fix now and what to capture as an issue. Fix through `implement`. After any fix, run `just ci` again.

## 4. Open the pull request

```sh
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create --base main --title "<summary of the batch>" --fill
```

Write the body from the session task list. One bullet per task, in the order they were done.

```markdown
## Changes

- <task 1>
- <task 2>

## Verification

`just ci` passes. Reviewed with the `review` skill.
```

Add `Closes #N` only for tasks that had a real issue. Most sessions have none.

Request a review only when someone other than the author can give one. GitHub rejects a request for review from yourself, and this repo usually has one maintainer.

```sh
gh pr edit <N> --add-reviewer <login>
```

## 5. Hand off

gh pr create --base main --title "Make clubspot-sync able to complete a camp, and make the CRM navigable" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`clubspot-sync` had never completed a single camp in production. Every run since it was turned on
reported `programsChecked: 38, programsSynced: 0`. The 38 camps failed in three classes that
partitioned the set exactly (11 + 13 + 14), across 380 failure events in 30 days.

Because `applyPlan` writes each collection as it is planned, with no transaction around a camp, the
CRM already held partially-synced camps — programs for all 38, and people, registrations and
registration entries for the 14 that reached billing.

Design: `.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md`.

## The failure classes

| Class | Camps | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 11 | A dateless `CampSession` crashed `toDateString`. Legacy records; Clubspot's UI requires both dates today. (#131) |
| B | 13 | An entry cap pointed at a session the archived filter excludes, so `requireLookup` threw. |
| C | 14 | `registration_billing.currency` rejected as required. |

Class C was not bad data. `queryCampEntries` never included `billing_registration`, so the pointer
was unfetched and every `get` on it returned `undefined`. `centsOrZero` silently turned all twelve
money fields into `0`, and only `currency` had no fallback. **The 400 was the only thing keeping a
table of fake zero billing out of the CRM.**

## Changes

- Move the scheduled sync from every six hours to hourly. `BASE_INTERVAL_MS` moves with the cron —
  leaving it at six hours would have made every camp skip on five of every six runs.
- Fetch `billing_registration`, and refuse an unfetched pointer instead of writing zeros.
- Make `sessions.start_date` / `end_date` nullable, and fix the two consumers that blocks:
  `roster.ts` throws naming the session, `todo-manager` skips it and continues. Neither was correct
  before — `DateTime.fromJSDate(undefined)` yields an invalid DateTime rather than throwing.
- Skip an entry cap or registration entry whose session cannot be resolved, warning with every id
  needed to find the row later. `requireLookup` still throws for program and class references.
- Add `sessions.archived`, and `--include-archived` to reach archived sessions for a manual
  backfill. Scheduled runs still filter them.
- Make `registration_billing.currency` nullable, as the residual guard behind the fetch fix.
- Add `programs_skipped` / `programs_failed` to `sync_runs` and `items_skipped` to
  `sync_program_runs`. A run where every camp was skipped by backoff previously reported `ok` with
  no indication anything was wrong.
- Grant Directus admin access to one account, as a deliberate per-account exception. The Staff role
  is unchanged.
- Set a `display_template` on all 16 CRM collections. Every one was `null`, so relational fields
  rendered primary keys — a person's `contact_links` showed UUIDs.
- Allow parallel sub-agent dispatch when file sets are disjoint, replacing the one-writer-at-a-time
  rule. The git index is the real shared constraint, so every agent stages explicit paths.

## Verification

`just ci` passes: 19 test files, 231 tests, 0 errors. The 12 `no-explicit-any` warnings are
pre-existing in files this branch does not touch.

Steps touching the schema were each verified against a live local Directus via `just directus-local`
— including that a token-authenticated `readItems` on `sessions` still returns archived rows after
`archive_field` is set, so reconciliation cannot duplicate them.

A `review` pass over the full diff is in progress; findings will be addressed on this branch.

## Deploy note

`scripts/deploy` applies `infrastructure` (the job image) before `crm` (the schema), so there is a
window where new code meets the old columns. That failure is the same contained per-camp failure and
self-heals on the next hourly run. All three nullability changes drop NOT NULL and the new column
has a default, both the safe direction.

No backfill is needed for recovery: `watermarkForCamp` reads the newest `ok` program run, and no
camp has one, so every watermark is still the epoch and the first successful run re-reads everything.

## Follow-ups

- Run `--include-archived` against one camp to verify it, and to learn whether Class B's missing
  sessions were archived or deleted — the warning disappears if archived, persists if deleted. Not
  yet exercised against live Clubspot data.
- Then backfill the 13 Class B camps with `--camp <id> --include-archived`, dry run first.
- #134 — `registration_billing`'s display template renders raw cents.
- #135 — `readSharedTables` reads ten collections in full every run, now hourly.

Fixes the code side of #131, which is closed with the detail of why nullable dates were chosen over
the skip that issue proposed.
EOF
