Stop a failure inside `runSync`'s error handling from stranding the run log.

Working tree: /Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync (branch session/people-sync). Work only there. No other agents are running — the tree is yours.

## The bug

A code review found two linked problems in `runSync` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-run.ts`).

**1. A throw from inside the `catch` block escapes the camp loop.** The `catch` that handles a failed camp calls `syncLog.recordProgramRun(...)`. If that call throws, it throws from inside the catch, so the loop does not continue to the next camp and the whole run aborts. The one camp's failure becomes every camp's.

**2. There is no `finally`, so `finishRun` is skipped.** When anything escapes the loop, `finishRun` never runs and the `sync_runs` row is left at `status: "running"` forever, with no `finished_at` and no error. From the outside that is indistinguishable from a run still in progress.

Concrete trigger: `scripts/deploy` applies the job image before the schema, so in that window `startRun`'s insert carries columns Directus does not have yet and returns a 400. More generally any Directus hiccup mid-run does it.

## Task

Make two guarantees hold:

- **A camp's failure stays that camp's failure.** If recording a program run fails — for either the failed-camp path or the skipped-camp path — log it and carry on to the next camp. The camp should still count as failed in the run totals.
- **The `sync_runs` row always gets closed.** Whatever happens in the loop, `finishRun` runs, with an accurate status and an error that names what went wrong.

Decide the structure yourself. Two things to get right rather than paper over:

- If `finishRun` itself throws, that is genuinely unrecoverable and should surface — do not swallow it into silence. But it must not mask an earlier, more informative error from the loop.
- The dry-run path must keep working. A dry run's `startRun` never reaches Directus, so `run.id` is undefined and `runId` falls back to `"dry-run"`. Do not make the new error handling assume a real id.

`RunSyncResult` still needs to carry accurate `programsChecked`, `programsSynced`, `programsSkipped`, `programsFailed` and `failedCampIds` when the run ends abnormally.

## Scope fence

| B | 13 | An entry cap pointed at a session the archived filter excludes, so `requireLookup` threw. |
| C | 14 | `registration_billing.currency` rejected as required. |

**Class C was not bad data.** `queryCampEntries` never included `billing_registration`, so the
pointer was unfetched and every `get` on it returned `undefined`. `centsOrZero` silently turned all
twelve money fields into `0`, and only `currency` had no fallback. The 400 was the only thing
keeping a table of fake zero billing out of the CRM — had currency been nullable from the start,
there would be 14 camps of financial data reading zero with no error anywhere.

## Sync changes

- Hourly instead of every six hours. `BASE_INTERVAL_MS` moves with the cron, plus a small tolerance:
  a run's `now` is captured at action start while its `started_at` is recorded after ten full table
  reads, so an exact-interval comparison made an active camp due only every *other* run.
- Fetch `billing_registration`, and refuse an unfetched pointer rather than write zeros.
- `sessions.start_date` / `end_date` nullable, and the two consumers that blocks fixed:
  `roster.ts` throws naming the session, `todo-manager` skips and continues. Neither was correct
  before — `DateTime.fromJSDate(undefined)` yields an invalid DateTime rather than throwing.
- Skip an entry cap or registration entry whose session cannot be resolved, warning with every id
  needed to find the row. `requireLookup` still throws for program and class references.
- `sessions.archived`, plus `--include-archived` to reach archived sessions for a manual backfill.
  Scheduled runs still filter them.
- `registration_billing.currency` nullable, as the residual guard behind the fetch fix.
- A participant-less registration now warns and counts instead of vanishing silently.
- `programs_skipped` / `programs_failed` on `sync_runs`, `items_skipped` on `sync_program_runs`. A
  run where every camp was skipped by backoff previously reported `ok` with nothing to indicate it.
- A camp's failure can no longer strand the run: recording a program run is guarded, and `finishRun`
  always closes the `sync_runs` row rather than leaving it at `status: running`.

## CRM usability

- `display_template` on all 16 collections. Every one was `null`, so relational fields rendered
  primary keys — a person's `contact_links` showed UUIDs.
- Directus admin access granted to one account as a deliberate per-account exception. The Staff role
  is unchanged.

## Workflow and docs

- Sub-agents may now be dispatched in parallel when their file sets are disjoint, replacing the
  one-writer-at-a-time rule. The git index is the real shared constraint, so every agent stages
  explicit paths.
- Comments must not cite `.claude/plans/` — those are session artifacts that get deleted when work
  lands. 21 such citations were rewritten to carry their own reasoning; 4 dangling path references
  were fixed. `docs/` references and issue numbers stay fine.
- Deleted three finished plan docs and `crm-schema.md`'s field tables (redundant with
  `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, and hand-updated twice on this branch alone). `crm-schema.md` keeps the
  merge procedure, provenance, auth identity and permission model. `docs/architecture.md` pruned of
  content the code now contradicts.

Net **−435 lines** across 47 files.

## Verification

`just ci` passes: 19 test files, 234 tests, 0 errors. The 12 `no-explicit-any` warnings are
pre-existing in files this branch does not touch.

Every schema change was verified against a live local Directus via `just directus-local` — including
that a token-authenticated `readItems` on `sessions` still returns archived rows once `archive_field`
is set, so reconciliation cannot duplicate them.

Reviewed with the `review` skill. Seven findings, all addressed: three were real bugs (the backoff
boundary, the stranded run log, the uncounted registration skip — the last of which revealed that
`items_skipped` could never have counted a dropped registration at all), two were stale comments,
one was an over-promise in the README, and one was accepted as-is with reasons below.

## Deploy note

`scripts/deploy` applies `infrastructure` (the job image) before `crm` (the schema), so there is a
window where new code meets old columns. `startRun` writes the new counter columns, so a run
triggered in that window fails before touching a camp — contained, and it self-heals on the next
hourly run now that `finishRun` always closes the row. All nullability changes drop NOT NULL and the
new columns have defaults, both the safe direction.

No recovery backfill is needed: `watermarkForCamp` reads the newest `ok` program run, and no camp has
one, so every watermark is still the epoch and the first successful run re-reads everything.

## Follow-ups

- **Verify `--include-archived`** against one of the 13 Class B camps. It has never been run against
  live Clubspot data. That single dry run also answers whether those sessions were archived or
  deleted: the warning disappears if archived, persists if deleted.
- **Then backfill** the Class B camps with `--camp <id> --include-archived`, dry run first.
- #134 — `registration_billing`'s display template renders raw cents.
- #135 — `readSharedTables` reads ten collections in full every run, now hourly.

## Accepted as-is

- Partial writes per camp. Directus REST has no cross-collection transaction; camps converge on the
  next successful run.
- `sessions.archive_field` makes the Data Studio delete button a soft delete that the next sync
  undoes. Intended — Clubspot is the source of truth, and the README now says so rather than
  promising manual edits survive.
- `buildRegistrationBillingRow` throws rather than skips on an unfetched billing pointer. It is the
  only detector for a regression that removes the `include`, and there is no evidence of a genuinely
  dangling pointer in this data.
- A session archived in Clubspot *after* being synced keeps `archived: false`, since scheduled runs
  stop fetching it. Acceptable — once archived there, it no longer needs syncing.
- `docs/architecture.md`'s cost figures are derived from code comments, not billing, and are
  unverified.

Fixes the code side of #131, closed with the detail of why nullable dates were chosen over the skip
that issue proposed.

## The deploy failed partway, and production is now in a bad state

**What failed:** both `DirectusUser` dynamic resources errored on update — `crm-clubspot-sync-user` with `Unexpected struct type.` and `crm-staff-ungood` with `error: undefined`. **Why it matters right now:** the `clubspot-sync` image was pushed and replaced *before* the failure. The Cloud Run job references it by mutable tag (`imageTag`, no digest), so it resolves at execution time. **The new code is live. The schema is not** — the `crm` project never ran, because `infrastructure` failed first.

So on the next hourly trigger, `startRun` will write `programs_skipped` and `programs_failed` into a table that doesn't have them, get a 400, and die before touching any camp. That's exactly the deploy-window hazard the PR describes, except it's now open indefinitely rather than for an hour.

It is not data corruption — the run writes nothing at all — and the sync was already 0-for-38, so no outcome is worse than yesterday. But it won't recover on its own.

**Two ways forward, and I want your call because one touches prod again immediately:**

1. **Apply the `crm` schema alone, now.** That closes the window — the new columns exist, the live code works, and the schema change is purely additive so old code is unaffected either way. Then fix the `DirectusUser` bug and re-run the full deploy for the scheduler and admin policy.
2. **Diagnose first, deploy nothing.** Leaves the sync dead until fixed, which is where it already was.

I lean strongly toward 1 — it's additive, it makes live code and live schema agree, and it's the smaller of the two prod actions.

Let me look at the actual bug while you decide.

content.text:
## Diagnosis

`DirectusUser`'s `update` returns:

```ts
return { outs: { ...news, userId: olds.userId, adopted: olds.adopted } satisfies DirectusUserOutputs };
```

Every field of `DirectusUserInputs` is spread in, including the optional ones — and each of the two resources has exactly one optional field that is `undefined`:

- `crm-clubspot-sync-user` is a machine user: `externalIdentifier` is `undefined`
- `crm-staff-ungood` is an OIDC user: `token` is `undefined`

`olds.adopted` can also be `undefined` — the code comments even say so, for state written before adoption existed.

Pulumi marshals a dynamic resource's `outs` into a protobuf struct, and `undefined` isn't a representable struct value. Hence `Unexpected struct type.` on one and a message-less `error: undefined` on the other — two different undefined keys, two different failure paths. `create` has the same shape but was never exercised with these values.

This is latent, not new. What this branch did was add a class to `resources.ts`, which re-serialized the shared dynamic-provider closure and forced an update on two resources whose own properties hadn't changed — walking straight into it. Adjacent to #125, which already records this area being fragile on delete.

Dispatching the fix now, since it needs no production access.

## The request, in the user's words

"I want some custom field definitions to be 'promoted' to People fields. The way I think this can work is that we add a 'Promoted Fields' collection in Directus where each row gives the People field name to populate and a list of Custom Field Definition _labels_ that should match. So: a config collection, maintained by staff, mapping one target `people` field to a set of source labels. Ship it with `School` only.

## What is already true

- `custom_field_definitions` is **per camp**, not per club — the same logical question gets one row per camp, and its label can drift between clones. That is why matching on label rather than id is the user's instinct, and it is the right one.

- `packages/crm/schema.yaml` is the Directus schema, applied by Pulumi. It manages **collections and fields, not rows.**

## Decisions the design must settle

Work these out and recommend; do not leave them all as open questions.

1. **Where promotion runs.** Inside `clubspot-sync` as a pass after registrations, as its own pass, or outside it entirely — a Directus Flow, or a separate job. Weigh it against the package's existing shape: pure plan functions with a thin executor, testable without Parse or Directus.
2. **Conflict resolution.** A person registers for three camps across two years and answers "School" differently each time. Which value wins? Most recent registration is the obvious candidate — say what "most recent" keys on, and what happens on a tie.
3. **Whether promotion overwrites a manual edit.** `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` now states that Clubspot is the source of truth for synced columns and a manual edit is overwritten, with person references the one exception. Decide whether a promoted column follows that rule or is treated as staff-owned once set, and make the README consistent with whatever you choose.
4. **How the target field is named.** A row holding a `people` column name as free text is stringly typed and silently breaks if the column is renamed or misspelled. Consider what Directus offers instead, and what happens when a row names a column that does not exist.

6. **How the `School` row gets there.** Pulumi manages schema, not rows, so a config row is either created by hand in the Data Studio or seeded somehow. Say which, and if seeding, where that lives.

Here's the gap. **Clubspot's `registration_campSession` join object carries seven fields; the CRM stores one derived string.**

`RegistrationCampSessionAttributes` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:511-530`):

| Clubspot field | Synced? |
|---|---|
| `status` | ❌ — ignored in favour of a derived value |
| `confirmed_at` | ❌ |
| `waitlist` | only as an input to the derived status |
| `waitlistNumber` | ❌ |
| `acceptedFromWaitlist` | ❌ |
| `priority` | ❌ |
| `waitlist_updates` (array) | ❌ |

`RegistrationEntryRow` (`packages/crm/src/registrations.ts:17`) holds only `registration_id`, `session_id`, `class_id`, `status`, `clubspot_session_join_id`.

And the derived `status` is lossier than it looks. `calculateEntryStatus` (`registrations.ts:45`) collapses everything to `cancelled` / `waitlist` / `confirmed`, and **two of its branches warn and then discard the distinction anyway** — an unrecognised registration status becomes `confirmed`, and a recognised-but-not-confirmed status also becomes `confirmed` with a warning. So today you cannot tell waitlist position, whether someone was accepted off the waitlist, or when an individual entry was confirmed as opposed to when the registration was.

Two decisions change what I build, so I'd rather ask than guess:

options.label: Replace derived with raw

options.description: One `waitlist_updates` JSON column holding the array as-is. Cheap, ships with everything else, and readable in the Data Studio. Not queryable or filterable per update, and not reportable in Insights.

options.label: Its own child collection
options.description: A `waitlist_updates` collection with an FK to registration_entries, one row per update. Queryable, filterable, chartable — and the right shape if you ever want waitlist movement over time. A larger change: new collection, new plan function, its own reconcile and cancel semantics.

That pins it exactly. The thrown value reaching `describeProviderError` is a **plain object with `status: 400` and no `message` and no `stack`** — which is why the fallback printed `[object Object]`.

Clubspot's `registration_campSession` join object carries seven fields (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:511-530`). ## Task

**1. Add these columns to `registration_entries`** in `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, to `RegistrationEntryRow`, and to the mapping in `planRegistrationEntries` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:164`):

| Column | Source on the join object | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clubspot_status` | `status` | Clubspot's own per-entry status, stored verbatim |
| `confirmed_at` | `confirmed_at` | timestamp, nullable — the SDK types it optional |
| `waitlist_number` | `waitlistNumber` | integer, nullable |
| `accepted_from_waitlist` | `acceptedFromWaitlist` | boolean, nullable |
| `priority` | `priority` | integer, nullable |

**Every one of these is nullable, and a missing value is written as null — never defaulted.** That is this repo's settled policy: a missing scalar makes the column nullable, and nothing is fabricated. `priority` is typed as required in the SDK, but the SDK's types have already been wrong about `startDate`, `endDate`, `currency`, `weight` and `pcpName` in live data, so do not trust it — make it nullable too. A `0` for an absent priority is an invented value.

Do **not** sync `waitlist_updates`. The user decided to skip it, and does not want an issue filed for it.

**2. Keep the derived `status` exactly as it is.** Everything already reads those three values (`cancelled` / `waitlist` / `confirmed`), and `clubspot_status` now carries the raw value alongside. Do not change what `status` means.

**3. Make an unrecognized registration status throw.** `calculateEntryStatus` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:45`) currently warns and returns `"confirmed"` when the status is not in `KNOWN_REGISTRATION_STATUSES`. That is a silent-defaulting path the user wants gone — their words: "I want an unknown status to FAIL syncs; this is something I want to catch and fix rather than silently ignore."

Replace that branch with a throw whose message names the unrecognized status and enough ids to find the row. The camp will then fail and be logged, which is the intended behavior — `runSync` already contains a per-camp failure.

**Leave the *other* warning in that function alone** — the one for a status that is recognized but not `confirmed`. That value is known, it is now also stored verbatim in `clubspot_status`, and only the unknown case was asked for.

Touch only: `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/registrations.ts`, `packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts`, `packages/clubspot-sync/test/registrations.test.ts`, and `packages/clubspot-sync/test/sync-run.test.ts` only if a fixture there needs the new columns to keep compiling.

Do not touch `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/`, `src/crm/`, `src/bootstrap/`, or anything outside `packages/infrastructure/`.

- **Acceptable: a skip that is counted and logged** with enough ids to find the row. That is the established pattern — `items_skipped` on `sync_program_runs`, plus a `winston.warn` naming the ids.
- **Also acceptable: a null.** A nullable column holding null is honest about not knowing. The repo's settled policy is that a missing scalar becomes nullable and nothing is fabricated.

Here's the detail. **The README line I had rewritten is wrong, and `fillGapsPatch` is why.**

```ts
if (incomingValue === undefined || incomingValue === null) continue;
if (existing[key] === null || existing[key] === undefined) patch[key] = incomingValue;
```

It only writes into columns that are **empty**. It never overwrites a value that's already there. And it's used for every `people` write (`person-sync.ts:74` and `:90`).

So the real behaviour today is: **for `people`, the first value wins, a staff edit is permanent, and a later change in Clubspot never lands.** The README now claims the opposite — that Clubspot is the source of truth and manual edits are overwritten, with person references the sole exception. That's false for `people`'s own columns too. I'll fix it once you've picked, since the fix depends on your answer.

**Your three options for promoted `school`:**

**Gap-fill** — matches `fillGapsPatch`, so `people` behaves uniformly. First promoted school sticks; you can correct it and the correction is permanent. Cost: a genuine school change never lands. A kid who answers "Garfield" in 2024 and "Roosevelt" in 2026 keeps Garfield forever.

**Overwrite** — the most recent registration always wins, so school changes land automatically. Cost: it wipes your corrections every hour. You fix a parent's typo, the sync reverts it within the hour. Given the whole reason you want a cleanup UX is to correct this data by hand, this one fights the goal directly.

**Overwrite only when the source changed** — remember what was last promoted; if Clubspot's answer differs from that, overwrite, otherwise leave the column alone. School changes land, and your corrections survive until the underlying answer actually changes. Cost: one extra column per promoted field to hold the last-promoted source value, and more logic to get wrong.

**My recommendation: gap-fill now.** You're about to hand-clean this data, and gap-fill is the only option that doesn't fight you while you do it. A stale school is visible and fixable; an hourly revert is not. If stale values become the real problem later, the third option is a contained upgrade — and by then you'll know whether it's worth the extra column.

Both fixes are running. Once they're in: backfill all 13 camps with the full archived history, as you asked.

## Confirmed findings

### 1. The registration watermark is later than the window it closes — rows in the gap are never synced, ever

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-run.ts:501` and `:524`, with `/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:12-17`

The registration query window is `[watermark, now)` where `now` is captured in `main.ts` at action start. The watermark for the next run is `max(started_at)` over the camp's `ok` rows — and `started_at` is `new Date()` captured inside the camp loop, i.e. *after* `startRun`, `priorProgramRuns`, `discoverCamps`, `readSharedTables`, and every camp synced before this one. So `started_at > now`, always, and the interval `(now, started_at)` is covered by no window in any run.

`backoff.ts:9-16` already documents that `started_at` lags the trigger, which is the same fact viewed from the other side.

Failure case: an hourly run starts at 10:00:00 and reaches camp #20 at 10:03:30, recording `started_at: 10:03:30`; its fetch used `updatedAt < 10:00:00`. A parent confirms a registration at 10:01:00. The 11:00 run's window starts at 10:03:30, so that registration is outside every window. Registrations are typically written once and never touched again, so it is permanently absent from the CRM — `items_skipped` 0, run status `ok`, nothing logged.

Smallest fix: pass `startedAt` rather than `now` as the `until` bound at `sync-run.ts:524`, so windows tile exactly. Note that `test/sync-run.test.ts:239` and `:277` currently assert the buggy bound, and `README.md:112` documents it, so both move with the fix.

### 2. `centsOrZero` fabricates money for eleven fields the SDK says are always present

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:250-252`, used at `:274-284`

Confirming your item 2, with a sharper line than "is 0 defensible": `BillingRegistrationAttributes` (clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:135-152) types `amount`, `amountPending`, `amountRefunded`, `amount_capturable`, `amount_deferred`, `amount_received`, `application_fee_amount`, `discount`, `processingFee`, `processing_passed_on`, and `tax` as **required**. For those eleven, an absent value on a *fetched* billing object means the SDK's model of Clubspot is wrong — exactly the case you want to fail. Only `deferredAmountBilled?` is genuinely optional, and `0` there reads honestly ("nothing billed yet").

Failure case: Clubspot renames `amount_received` (it already mixes camelCase and snake_case in this one class, so a rename is the likeliest breakage). Every billing row silently reads `amount_received: 0`, `amount_pending` unchanged, and staff chase payments from families who already paid.

Two options, different sizes: small — throw for the eleven required fields, naming `registration.id` and `billing.id`, keeping `?? 0` only for `deferredAmountBilled`. Large — make the columns nullable, which is a `schema.yaml` change across twelve fields plus `RegistrationBillingRow` plus every reader, and loses the `default_value: 0` that currently makes them sane. I'd take the throw; it matches the `isDataAvailable()` guard right above it.

### 3. `first_name ?? ""` creates a nameless person, and then matches other nameless people to it

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:257`

`people.first_name` is NOT NULL and `required: true`, and `ParticipantAttributes.firstName` is optional, so the mapping papers over the mismatch with `""`. Worse than a blank cell: `normalizeName("")` returns `null`, so in `matchParticipant` (`people.ts:154-166`) a nameless incoming participant compares equal on first name to **every** stored nameless person.

Failure case: two different campers registered with only a last name and the same date of birth (or a camp where the form didn't collect first names) collapse into one `people` row, and the second camper's medical profile overwrites the first's via `syncMedicalProfile`'s `diffFields` tracking. That is the "false merge silently attaches one family's medical data to another person" outcome `docs/crm-schema.md:52-54` says the matcher exists to prevent.

Smallest fix: throw in `buildPersonFieldsFromParticipant` when `firstName` is absent, naming the participant id. There is no honest fallback for a NOT NULL name.

### 4. `registrations.status ?? ""` writes an empty status, and contradicts the throw added one function away

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:97` (confirming your item 4; `:186` is the sibling `?? ""`)

`registrations.status` is NOT NULL and `required: true`. A status-less registration is written with `status: ""`, which renders in Directus as a real (blank) status. It is also now internally inconsistent: `:186` feeds the same `""` into `calculateEntryStatus`, which since `9fb40e6b` throws on it. So the row is created with `status: ""`, then the camp fails on the first session join, leaving the fabricated row behind with no entries.

Related stale prose at `registrations.ts:38-42`: "or no status at all — can reach here on a registration that already has a `confirmed_at`. All fold to `confirmed`." After `9fb40e6b`, no status at all does not fold to anything; it throws. The comment now describes the behavior the commit deliberately removed.

Smallest fix: throw in `buildRegistrationRow` for an absent status, alongside the existing `confirmed_at` throw, and delete the "or no status at all" clause. A registration with no `status` then fails whether or not it has join objects, which is what you asked for.

### 5. `waitlist ?? false` should throw — nothing breaks today

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:217` (your item 1)

Failure case: Clubspot stops setting `waitlist` on join objects (or sets it only when true, which is how `archived` behaves). Every waitlisted camper reads `status: confirmed` in the CRM while `waitlist_number` sits populated right beside it, and staff hand out seats that do not exist. The internal contradiction is detectable, which is what makes the fabrication dangerous rather than merely wrong.

What breaks if it throws: nothing, on today's data — every observed join object carries the flag, which is why the SDK types it required. If Clubspot ever drops it, camps with waitlisted entries fail loudly, naming registration and join ids. That is the behavior you asked for.

### 6. `sessions.archived` can only be set true by a manual backfill flag

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:136`, with `/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:76-80`

The only code path that can ever write `archived: true` is a human running `--camp X --include-archived`. This is the `default_value` fiction you asked about, in its live form: `sessions.archived` is `false` on every row the scheduled sync maintains, and `sessions` uses `archived` as its Directus `archive_field` (`schema.yaml:359-365`), so the Data Studio treats those rows as live and shows them by default.

Failure case: staff archive "Week 7" in Clubspot. The hourly sync excludes it; the CRM keeps `Week 7` with `archived: false`, its `session_classes` links, and its registration entries intact. `items_skipped` stays 0 and nothing is logged. Only someone who happens to notice and runs the backfill flag corrects it.

Smallest fix: after `planSessions`, mark any existing CRM session for this program whose `clubspot_session_id` was not in the fetch as `archived: true` — the same "cancel, don't delete" shape `planRegistrationEntries` already uses for vanished join objects. (Modest change, one new pass plus a test.)

### 7. Classes and entry caps are fetched with no archived filter, and never removed

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:82-83`, with `/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:143-181`

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.handled/.../packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:365-368` — correct path: `/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:365-368`

### 9. Person matching decides on a truncated candidate set and cannot tell

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/person-sync.ts:24` and `:104-122`

The fallback fetch is `last_name _icontains <lastName>` with `limit: 50`. `_icontains` is a substring match, so a short last name matches far more than itself, and when the real row falls outside the 50 the code cannot distinguish "no match" from "match beyond the cap" — it creates a duplicate person silently.

Smallest fix: warn when `candidates.length === CANDIDATE_LIMIT` and no match was found, naming the filter used — the decision was made on a truncated set, and that is the one case worth an operator's eye.

### 10. `findAll` treats a short page as the last page

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/parse-paging.ts:17-25` (your item 5)

A rejected `find()` does surface — it propagates to the camp catch and is recorded `failed`, so an outright paging failure is handled. Truncation is not fully closed, though. The loop stops when `page.length < pageSize`, which assumes the server honored the requested limit. Parse Server has a `maxLimit` setting that silently clamps it; if Clubspot sets it below 1000, `findAll` gets a clamped first page, sees it as short, and returns it as complete — #128 again, one layer up. Separately, none of the paged queries sets a sort (`main.ts:76-87`), and `skip`-based paging over an unordered result can drop rows between pages.

Both are latent at today's volumes (~168 participants per camp, well under one page), so this is a durability fix rather than a live bug. Smallest fix: page until an empty page rather than a short one — one extra request per query, and it removes the assumption entirely.

### 11. Paged Directus reads are unsorted, and `custom_field_responses` has no unique constraint to catch a miss

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/directus.ts:93-104`

`limit: -1` pages with `page=N` and no `sort`, so ordering across pages is whatever Postgres gives. For most collections a missed existing row is caught loudly: `clubspot_registration_id`, `clubspot_session_join_id`, `clubspot_entry_cap_id`, `registration_billing.registration_id` are all unique, so a re-create 400s and the camp is recorded `failed`. `custom_field_responses` has no unique constraint on `(registration_id, definition_id)`, so a missed row there becomes a duplicate answer row, silently. Same for `response?.data ?? []` at `:99` turning an unexpected body into "no rows".

Smallest fix: add `sort: ["id"]` to the `limit: -1` path so paging is deterministic.

### 12. `reusePerson` proceeds silently when the pinned person no longer exists

`/Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/people-sync/packages/clubspot-sync/src/person-sync.ts:71-80`

If the read returns nothing, the method returns `{ id: personId, created: false }` anyway and the caller writes medical and contact data against an id that is not in `people`.

Failure case: staff do step 4 of the merge procedure (`docs/crm-schema.md:60-66`) — delete the duplicate — while a `contacts` row still points at it. The FK is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so the dependent rows vanish; the next sync re-reads nothing, silently treats the dead id as valid, and the participant's medical profile create fails on the FK with an error that names neither the participant nor the merge. A `winston.warn` at the `if (existing)` miss would name the participant and the stale id.

## The audit found a silent data-loss bug that predates this session

**The registration window has a permanent gap.** `fetchCampData`'s `until` bound is `now`, captured in `main.ts` at action start. But the next run's watermark is `max(started_at)` over `ok` runs, and `started_at` is captured *inside* the camp loop — after `startRun`, discovery, ten table reads, and every camp before it.

So `started_at > now`, always, and the interval between them is covered by **no window in any run**.

Concretely: a run starts 10:00:00 and reaches camp #20 at 10:03:30. Its fetch used `updatedAt < 10:00:00`; it records `started_at: 10:03:30`. A parent confirms a registration at 10:01:00. The 11:00 run's window starts at 10:03:30. That registration is outside every window that will ever run — and since registrations are written once and rarely touched, it never appears in the CRM. `items_skipped: 0`, status `ok`, nothing logged.

One-line fix: pass `startedAt` as the `until` bound so windows tile exactly. Two tests and one README line assert the current bound and move with it.

## Two more that mislead badly

**`first_name ?? ""` causes false merges.** `people.first_name` is NOT NULL but `ParticipantAttributes.firstName` is optional, so an absent name becomes `""`. Then `normalizeName("")` returns `null`, so in `matchParticipant` a nameless participant compares **equal on first name to every stored nameless person**. Two campers with only a last name and the same DOB collapse into one row, and the second's medical profile overwrites the first's. That is precisely the outcome `docs/crm-schema.md:52-54` says the matcher exists to prevent.

**`centsOrZero` fabricates money.** The SDK types eleven of the twelve amount fields as **required**, so an absent value on a *fetched* billing object means the SDK's model is wrong — your fail-loudly case exactly. Only `deferredAmountBilled` is genuinely optional, where `0` reads honestly. If Clubspot renames `amount_received` (that class already mixes camelCase and snake_case), every row silently reads `0` and staff chase families who already paid.

| 10-12 | `findAll` treats a clamped page as the last; unsorted paged reads; `reusePerson` proceeds on a dead id | issue |

gh issue create --title "Manual edits in Directus permanently disable syncing for that field" --label "enhancement,P2" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`fillGapsPatch` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts`) only writes into a column that is empty:

```ts
if (existing[key] === null || existing[key] === undefined) patch[key] = incomingValue;
```

It is used for every `people` write (`person-sync.ts:74`, `:90`), and `docs/crm-schema.md:57-59`
documents the behavior deliberately — it is what makes a manual merge durable.

The consequence is not intended, though: **once a field has any value, Clubspot can never update it
again.** Staff cleaning up data in the Data Studio silently switch off syncing for every field they
touch, permanently and invisibly. A camper who changes school, phone number, or address keeps the
old value forever, and nothing records that an incoming update was dropped.

That is the wrong model. Cleaning data should not mean opting a row out of the sync.

## Scope

All `people` scalar columns, and the promoted fields in `.claude/plans/promoted-fields.md` —
`school` ships with gap-fill for consistency with the above, and inherits the same problem.

Not in scope: `registrations.person_id` / `contacts.person_id`, which are pinned at creation for a
different and good reason (a repointed FK must survive, or a manual merge would be undone).

## Possible approaches

- **Three-way merge.** Remember the last value the sync wrote per field. Overwrite when Clubspot's
  value differs from that; leave the column alone when it is unchanged. A staff correction survives
  until the source answer actually changes. Costs a per-field record of what was last synced.
- **Per-field provenance.** Mark each column as sync-owned or staff-owned, and let staff take
  ownership explicitly rather than implicitly by typing in it.
- **Overwrite plus visible history.** Let Clubspot win, and surface the overwritten value so a
  correction is not silently lost. Directus revisions may cover most of this already.

Whatever is chosen, an incoming update that is dropped should be counted and logged — right now it
is neither.

## Impact

Gets worse as staff use the CRM. The data-cleanup UX in #133 will actively create these dead
fields, so this should be settled before that work lands rather than after.

Also: `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` currently claims Clubspot is the source of truth for synced
columns and that a manual edit is overwritten, with person references the only exception. That is
false for every `people` scalar. Correct it as part of this, or sooner.
EOF
)"

# Capture an Issue

Turn a problem — from the current conversation or the user's description — into a well-formed GitHub issue in `cyc-seattle/isthmia`.

## When to file one

File an issue when the work will outlive the current session: a problem found mid-task that you
are deliberately not fixing now, a known defect with no owner, or work that needs to be scheduled.

Do **not** file an issue for work you are about to do in this session. The session's pull request
records it. See the Workflow section of `CLAUDE.md`.

## Steps

1. **Gather the problem.** Pull details from the conversation or ask the user. A good issue needs: what's wrong or wanted, where in the code (`path:line`), and why it matters.
2. **Check for duplicates first.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels`. If it overlaps an existing issue, tell the user and offer to comment on / rescope that one instead of filing a new duplicate.
3. **Pick a type label:** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, or `docker`.
4. **Assign a priority label** using the rubric below.
5. **Write the body** using the template below. Reference concrete files as `path:line`.
6. **Create it:** `gh issue create --title "<imperative title>" --label "<type>,<priority>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`
7. **Report** the issue number and URL back to the user.

## Priority rubric (P0–P3)

- **P0 — Critical:** data integrity/corruption, production broken, or a security-critical hole. Work starts immediately.
- **P1 — High:** a significant bug or friction the user hits regularly, with no safe workaround (e.g. auth/tooling breakage).
- **P2 — Medium:** a real improvement or a bug with a workaround (added tests, hardening, moderate bugs).
- **P3 — Low:** cleanup, docs, polish, low-risk nice-to-haves.

## Body template

Keep it tight. Use `## Problem` always; then `## Fix` (bugs) or `## Proposed changes` / `## Scope` (enhancements); add `## Impact` when the "why" isn't obvious.

```markdown
## Problem

<what's wrong/wanted, with `path:line` references and a code snippet if useful>

## Fix

<concrete change; mention adding a regression test for bugs>

## Impact

<why it matters — omit if self-evident>
```

## Conventions

- **Title:** short, imperative, no priority prefix (priority lives in the label). e.g. "safeCall retries non-retryable errors with a 60s delay".
- Labels already exist: `P0`–`P3`, `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `docker`. Don't invent new ones without asking.
- For bugs, always note that the fix should include a regression test — tests live in `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`.
- Cross-link related issues with `#N` and note dependencies ("land #47 first").

Earlier on this branch, the one-writer-at-a-time rule was replaced with a rule for deciding: parallelize when file sets are disjoint, serialize on a shared file or package (and always on `packages/crm/schema.yaml`), and every agent stages explicit paths because the git index is shared. Using it for a day surfaced two hazards it does not cover. Both are real; both nearly caused damage.

## Hazard 1: never deploy while a writing sub-agent is active

`just deploy` builds the **working tree**, not `HEAD`. A deploy started while an agent has uncommitted edits on disk bakes half-finished code into a container image and applies a half-edited `packages/crm/schema.yaml` to production.

This was caught twice by checking `git status` first — once with four files mid-edit, including the schema. The same applies to anything that reads the tree rather than a commit: `just ci` and a local Directus apply included.

The rule: before a deploy, the tree must be clean. Wait for the agent, do not stash — the stash stack is shared with every other worktree, which the existing `git stash` guardrail already explains.

## Hazard 2: the pre-commit hook stashes the whole tree

`git commit` runs pre-commit, which **stashes all unstaged changes** for the hook run and restores them afterwards. So one agent committing briefly removes another agent's in-progress edits from disk, whatever paths either of them staged.

Observed as `[INFO] Restored changes from ~/.cache/pre-commit/patch<n>-<n>` during a commit while two other agents were writing. It restored correctly, and no loss was observed in a day of use — but "stage only your own paths" does not protect against it, because the hook operates tree-wide regardless of what is staged.

State it as a known hazard with the mitigation that actually helps: an agent that writes for a long time between commits widens the window, so prefer briefs that commit once and soon over ones that hold many files open. Do not overstate it — do not tell anyone to disable the hook.

gh pr edit 136 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`clubspot-sync` had never completed a single camp in production — every run since it was turned on
reported `programsChecked: 38, programsSynced: 0`, with 380 failure events in 30 days. Deployed from
this branch, it now completes camps. See **Production status** below.

Because `applyPlan` writes each collection as it is planned with no transaction around a camp, the
CRM already held partially-synced camps before any of this landed.

Designs: `.claude/plans/clubspot-sync-bad-data.md`, `.claude/plans/promoted-fields.md`.

## What was wrong

Every failure had the same shape: **the SDK types a field as required, live Clubspot data disagrees,
and the CRM column is NOT NULL** — so the row is rejected and the camp dies. Seven fields turned out
to be wrong that way: `startDate`, `endDate`, `name` on sessions; `currency` on billing; `value` on
custom field responses; and `firstName` on participants.

One was not a data problem at all. `queryCampEntries` never included `billing_registration`, so the
pointer was unfetched and every `get` on it returned `undefined`. `centsOrZero` turned all twelve
money fields into `0`, and only `currency` had no fallback. **The 400 error was the only thing
keeping a table of fake zero billing out of the CRM.**

## Sync correctness

- **The registration window had a permanent gap.** `until` was the run's start time, but the next
  watermark was each camp's `started_at`, recorded later — so the interval between them was covered
  by no window in any run, and a registration confirmed in it never reached the CRM. Both values are
  now the same `const` per camp, so the windows tile.
- Fetch `billing_registration`, and refuse an unfetched pointer rather than write zeros.
- Nullable where a value is legitimately absent: `sessions.start_date`, `end_date`, `name`,
  `registration_billing.currency`, `custom_field_responses.value`. Nothing is fabricated.
- **Throw where an absent value means the SDK is wrong**: unrecognized registration status, missing
  status or `confirmed_at`, a nameless participant, any of the eleven required billing amounts, a
  session join with no `waitlist` flag.
- Skip and count where a reference cannot be resolved: entry caps and registration entries pointing
  at an unknown session, participant-less registrations, answers to unknown custom fields.
- Archived sessions are now synced unconditionally and carry `archived: true`. Previously they were
  filtered out, which meant archiving in Clubspot never reached the CRM and 13 camps' entry caps
  could never resolve.
- A camp's failure can no longer strand the run: `finishRun` always closes the `sync_runs` row.
- Hourly instead of six-hourly, with a small tolerance — an exact-interval comparison made an active
  camp due only every *other* run.

## Visibility

- `programs_skipped` / `programs_failed` on `sync_runs`, `items_skipped` on `sync_program_runs`. A run
  where every camp was skipped by backoff previously reported `ok` with nothing to distinguish it.
- Five `registration_entries` columns Clubspot carried and the CRM discarded: `clubspot_status`,
  `confirmed_at`, `waitlist_number`, `accepted_from_waitlist`, `priority`.
- Person matching warns when it decided on a truncated candidate set, rather than silently creating a
  duplicate.
- `--dry-run` works on a camp with a new participant, so a run can be previewed.

## CRM usability

- `display_template` on all 16 collections. Every one was `null`, so relational fields rendered
  primary keys — a person's `contact_links` showed UUIDs.
- Directus admin access for one account as a per-account exception; the Staff role is unchanged.
  #138 will replace this with a manual grant from `master@`.

## Infrastructure reliability

Four production deploys failed before one succeeded, each on a different layer of the Directus
dynamic providers — all fixed here:

- `undefined` in a returned `outs` breaks Pulumi's protobuf marshalling.
- A thrown error crossing the provider boundary lost its message, surfacing as `error: undefined`.
  `Error.message` is non-enumerable, so serialization dropped it.
- `DirectusUser.update` could not recover from a stale stored id: its 404 re-resolution never fired,
  because Directus validates the payload first and returns 400 on a unique-email collision.
- Directus answers 403, not 404, for a user id that does not exist.

None of this is reachable by `pulumi preview` — dynamic providers only run on apply, and they have no
test coverage. #51 tracks the integration harness that would have caught all four.

## Workflow and docs

- Sub-agents may run in parallel when their file sets are disjoint. The git index is the shared
  constraint, so every agent stages explicit paths; never deploy or run `just ci` while an agent has
  uncommitted changes, since both build the tree rather than `HEAD`.
- Comments must not cite `.claude/plans/` — those are session artifacts. 21 such citations were
  rewritten to carry their own reasoning.
- Deleted three finished plan docs, `docs/architecture.md`'s obsolete sections, `crm-schema.md`'s
  field tables (redundant with `schema.yaml`), and unverifiable cost figures. `packages/crm/README.md`
  had the `schema.yaml` authoring direction backwards — the checked-in file is normative.

## Production status

Deployed from this branch. First successful run: **38 checked, 11 synced, 27 failed** — up from 0
synced, ever. The 27 were `sessions.name` and `custom_field_responses.value`, both now nullable and
deployed. Later runs are expected to complete more; the new throws may also surface camps that were
previously failing silently.

## Verification

`just ci` passes: 20 test files, 264 tests, 0 errors. The 12 `no-explicit-any` warnings are
pre-existing in files this branch does not touch.

Schema changes were verified against a live local Directus, except the last two
(`sessions.name`, `custom_field_responses.value`) where podman would not start — those rest on unit
tests plus a clean production apply.

Reviewed with the `review` skill (7 findings, all addressed) and a follow-up silent-failure audit
(12 findings: 6 fixed here, the rest filed).

## Follow-ups

- #137 — a manual edit in Directus permanently disables syncing for that field. `fillGapsPatch`
  gap-fills, so cleaning data opts a row out of the sync. Blocks #133.
- #138 — make `master@` the only IaC-declared Directus user.
- #134 — `registration_billing`'s display template renders raw cents.
- #135 — `readSharedTables` reads ten collections in full every run, now hourly.
- #133 — the Directus extension for cleaning up people data.
- Promoted fields (`school`) is designed and approved, not yet implemented.
- Audit findings not fixed here: `classes`/`entry_caps` are never removed when archived in Clubspot;
  `findAll` treats a clamped page as the last; paged Directus reads are unsorted; `reusePerson`
  proceeds on a dead person id.

Fixes the code side of #131, closed with the detail of why nullable dates were chosen over the skip
that issue proposed.
EOF

**What survives of that audit fix, and why the distinction matters:** the `isDataAvailable()` guard stays. Absent-means-zero and never-fetched are different failures. An absent `amount` is a real zero; a *present but unfetched* billing pointer means someone removed the `include` and *every* `get` returns undefined — which is the bug that silently zeroed all twelve fields for 14 camps and was the reason for that commit in the first place. Seven fields on this branch have turned out to be mistyped, and for most of them absent means a real value (`false`, `0`, `null`), not corruption. The heuristic that actually holds is narrower: throw when a value is *present but unrecognisable* (an unknown status), or when the *shape* is wrong (an unfetched pointer). Absent is usually just absent. I'll keep that in mind rather than re-deriving it next time the same reasoning looks compelling.
